definition_zh: 拥有；具备；支配；附身
definition_en: to own something, to have a quality or ability, or to control a person's mind as a spirit does
core_image: 一只手按在椅背上，以主人身份稳稳坐定
scene: 拍卖行的灯已经调暗，木槌悬在半空，围观的人屏住呼吸。 The collector possesses a small gold watch that once belonged to a railway engineer.
sceneCN: 这里 possess 是「拥有」（第 1 个义项：作为财产持有某物）；句意为这位收藏者拥有一只曾属于铁路工程师的小金表。画面里有调暗的灯、悬起的木槌和一只旧表。

pos.zh: 拥有；具备；支配；（鬼神）附身

collocations.zh: 你着了什么魔；你怎么会这样

derivatives.zh: possess 加表示「人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「拥有者；持有人」
possess 加 -ive 构成，义为「占有欲强的；所有格的」
self 与 possessed 复合，义为「沉着冷静的」，字面是「自我掌控的」

senses.title: To own something as property
senses.definition: to have something as your own property, especially something valuable or legally held
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为自己的财产持有，尤指贵重或依法持有的东西
senses.example: The family possesses two farms and a small orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人拥有两座农场和一小片果园。
senses.why: The Latin verb possidere pictured a master sitting over a place, so the earliest sense is holding property with authority rather than merely touching it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 possidere 的画面是主人坐在一处地方之上，所以最早的义项是带着支配意味地持有财产，而不只是碰到它。

senses.title: To have a quality or ability
senses.definition: to have a particular quality, skill or feature as part of what you are
senses.definitionCN: 作为自身的一部分而具备某种品质、技能或特征
senses.example: She possesses an unusual memory for faces.
senses.exampleCN: 她对人的面孔有非同寻常的记忆力。
senses.why: Once the word could hold a visible thing, it could hold an invisible one too: a quality is treated as something a person carries around.
senses.whyCN: 词一旦能「持有」看得见的东西，也就能「持有」看不见的东西：品质被看成人随身带着的一样东西。

senses.title: To take hold of someone's mind
senses.definition: of a feeling or idea, to fill someone's mind so strongly that it controls their behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或念头强烈占据某人的心神，以至于左右其行为
senses.example: A wild hope possessed him as he read the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 读那封信时，一个狂热的希望攫住了他。
senses.why: The step from owning objects to owning a mind is short: whatever fills your thoughts is felt as having moved in and taken the chair.
senses.whyCN: 从占有物品转到占有一个人的心神，只差一小步：凡是填满你念头的东西，都会被感觉成搬了进来、坐上了主位。

senses.title: To enter and control a person, as a spirit
senses.definition: of a spirit or demon, to enter a person and control what they say and do
senses.definitionCN: 指鬼魂或恶魔进入人体，控制其言行
senses.example: In the story a restless ghost possesses the youngest daughter.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，一个不安的鬼魂附上了最小的女儿。
senses.why: This is the literal picture behind the third sense: an outside power physically occupying a body, which was later borrowed as a metaphor for strong feeling.
senses.whyCN: 这是第三个义项背后的字面画面：一种外在力量实体般占据了身体，后来才被借去比喻强烈的情绪。

intro.en: Possess comes from a Latin verb that joins the idea of being able with the idea of sitting, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: possess 来自一个把「有能力」与「坐」合在一起的拉丁动词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The reconstructed root *poti- meant powerful or lord, and it is generally thought to lie behind the Latin words for ability and mastery.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 *poti- 表示「有力量的、主人」，拉丁语中表示能力与主宰的词都从它而来。

items.en: Latin joined potis, able or powerful, with sedere, to sit, making possidere, literally to sit as master over something.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 potis（有能力的、有权的）与 sedere（坐）合起来，构成 possidere，字面就是「以主人身份坐在某物之上」。

items.en: The noun possessio named both the act of holding and the thing held, and its stem possess- carried that meaning into the other forms of the family.
items.cn: 名词 possessio 既指持有的行为，也指被持有的东西，词干 possess- 把这一含义带进这一族的其他词形。

items.en: Old French possesser, recorded from the twelfth century, meant to own or to hold, and it entered English in the centuries after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古法语的 possesser 自十二世纪起有记录，意为拥有、持有，在诺曼人定居之后的几个世纪里进入英语。

items.en: Modern English kept the legal and everyday sense of owning, then extended the word to qualities a person has and to a spirit taking over a mind.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了法律与日常两种「拥有」义，再把词义扩展到人所具备的品质，以及鬼神占据一个人的心神。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the same Latin family of holding; the near-meaning group collects plainer verbs for having and keeping.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个表示「持有」的拉丁词族；近义组收更朴素地表示「有、留住」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun of state built on the same Latin stem, meaning the holding or the thing held.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词干上的名词，表示持有这一状态或被持有的东西。

entries.definition: An adjective for someone who tends to hold on to things or people.
entries.definitionCN: 形容总想把人或物抓在手里的。

entries.definition: The person who holds or owns something.
entries.definitionCN: 持有或拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: To take property or land away from someone by force or law.
entries.definitionCN: 以武力或法律手段剥夺某人的财产或土地。

entries.definition: To have something as your property, the plainest verb for it.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，是最朴素的说法。

entries.definition: To have something in your hands or under your control.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拿在手里，或置于自己控制之下。

entries.definition: The most general verb for something being yours or being with you.
entries.definitionCN: 最笼统的「有」，表示某物属于你或在你身边。

normalIntro.en: The word holds together a Latin adjective of power, a verb of sitting, and two English suffixes that turn it into a person and a tendency.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把表示权力的拉丁形容词、表示坐的动词，以及两个把它变成「人」和「倾向」的英语后缀箍在一起。

normal.en: Potis in Latin meant able or powerful, and sedere meant to sit, so possidere was to sit as master over a thing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为有能力的、有权的，sedere 意为坐，所以 possidere 就是坐在某物之上当主人。

normal.en: The double s is real: possess keeps the s of the Latin stem possess-, so it is never written posses or posess.
normal.cn: 双写 s 是真实的：possess 保留了拉丁词干 possess- 的 s，所以绝不写成 posses 或 posess。

normal.en: Possessor swaps the verb ending for -or, the suffix for a person, and names the one who holds.
normal.cn: possessor 把动词词尾换成表示人的 -or，指的就是持有的人。

normal.en: Possessive adds -ive, the suffix of tendency, so it describes a person inclined to hold on.
normal.cn: possessive 加的是表示倾向的 -ive，形容一个人总想抓住不放。

normal.en: Self-possessed uses the same verb in the sense of controlling oneself, and means calm rather than wealthy.
normal.cn: self-possessed 用的是这个词「掌控自己」的一面，意思是从容镇定，而不是富有。

abstract.en: Picture a hand resting flat on a chair arm: owning begins as the confidence to sit down and stay.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在扶手椅上：拥有最初就是一种敢坐下来、不走的底气。

abstract.en: A quality you possess is something invisible that you carry the way you carry a key.
abstract.cn: 你具备的品质，是一件看不见却随身带着的东西，像口袋里的一把钥匙。

abstract.en: The jump from owning a house to being owned by a fear shows how quickly holding turns into being held.
abstract.cn: 从拥有一栋房子，到被一种恐惧攫住，说明「抓住」与「被抓住」之间只隔一层。

examples.en: The collector possesses a small gold watch from the last century.
examples.cn: 这位收藏者拥有一只上世纪的小金表。

examples.en: He possesses a patience that surprises his students.
examples.cn: 他的耐心让他的学生感到惊讶。

examples.en: A sudden doubt possessed her at the door.
examples.cn: 站在门口时，一阵突如其来的疑虑攫住了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕塞死」——东西太多，柜子快被塞死，因为样样都想拥有；记住 possess 是拥有。

root: 拉丁语 potis（有能力的、有权的）与 sedere（坐）合成 possidere（以主人身份坐定、占有），经古法语 possesser 进入英语；同族词都围绕「持有、掌控」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is holding something with authority; the senses then reach from property to invisible qualities, to a mind taken over, and finally to a spirit in possession of a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是带着支配意味地持有某物；义项由此从财物伸向看不见的品质，再伸向被占据的心神，最后落到鬼神占据身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand resting on the arm of a chair, a master sitting firmly in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在椅子的扶手上，主人稳稳坐定。

branches.en: a deed folded inside a wooden box
branches.cn: 折好放在木盒里的地契

branches.en: a voice that remembers every face
branches.cn: 记得每一张面孔的嗓音

branches.en: a hope that will not leave the room
branches.cn: 赖在房间里不肯走的希望

branches.en: a cold draft passing through a locked door
branches.cn: 穿过锁着的门的一股冷风

branches.en: two farms and a talent, both called someone's own
branches.cn: 两座农场与一种才能，都被说成某人的

intro.en: A Latin adjective of power, a verb of sitting, and English suffixes for a person and a tendency carry the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个表示权力的拉丁形容词、一个表示坐的动词，加上表示人和倾向的英语后缀，撑起了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: potis, sedere, possidere and possessio all bear on this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的拉丁词有明确记录：potis、sedere、possidere 与 possessio 都与这个词有关。

definition_en: suddenly and by a large amount, in a severe way, or in a clear and distinct way
core_image: 折线在图表上突然向上折起
scene: 价格急剧上涨。 Prices rose sharply.

锐利；急剧

senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内大幅度地
senses.example: Prices rose sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 价格急剧上涨。
senses.why: This is the most common use in news and reports.
senses.whyCN: 这是新闻和报告中最常见的用法。

senses.title: Severely

senses.example: The teacher spoke sharply to the class.

senses.whyCN: 尖锐的语气像刀刃一样切割。

senses.title: Clearly

senses.example: The two colours contrast sharply.
senses.exampleCN: 两种颜色形成鲜明对比。
senses.why: A sharp outline is easy to see.

items.cn: sharply 形容数字的突然变化。

items.en: Sharply also marks a clear contrast.
items.cn: sharply 也标记鲜明的对比。

normalIntro.cn: sharply 给动词加上刀刃：价格向上切、话语切得深、线条切得分明。

normal.cn: 冬季销量急剧下降。

normal.en: She answered sharply.

normal.en: The road turns sharply left.
normal.cn: 道路向左急转。

normal.en: The two styles differ sharply.
normal.cn: 两种风格差别鲜明。

normal.en: He was sharply dressed.
normal.cn: 他穿得很利落。

abstract.en: A sharp change leaves a mark on the chart.
abstract.cn: 急剧变化会在图表上留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Sharp words are remembered longer than loud ones.
abstract.cn: 尖锐的话比大声的话被记得更久。

abstract.en: Clarity is a kind of sharpness.
abstract.cn: 清晰也是一种锋利。

root: 由 sharp（锋利）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，核心义「带刃地、急剧地」。

definition_zh: 专注；集中；浓度；聚集
definition_en: the ability to focus your attention, or the amount of a substance in a mixture
core_image: 一盏聚光灯把光全部打在一个点上
scene: 考场里安静得只剩笔尖划纸的声音。 Total concentration is needed for this kind of puzzle.
sceneCN: 这里 concentration 指「专注」（第 1 个义项：把注意力完全放在一件事上）；句意是解这类谜题需要全神贯注。

集中的；浓缩的
集中的；使专心的
浓缩器；集中器

senses.title: The power to focus
senses.definition: the ability to give all your attention to something
senses.definitionCN: 把全部注意力放在某事上的能力
senses.example: Reading in noise demands great concentration.
senses.exampleCN: 在噪声中阅读需要高度专注。
senses.why: The mind must hold one point and let the rest fade.
senses.whyCN: 心智必须守住一个点，让其余的都淡下去。

senses.title: A gathering in one place
senses.definition: the act of bringing many things together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把许多东西聚到一处
senses.example: The concentration of factories in the valley worried residents.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂聚集在山谷里，让居民担忧。
senses.why: People and things can be gathered just as light is gathered.
senses.whyCN: 人和物都能像光一样被收拢。

senses.title: Strength of a mixture
senses.definition: the amount of a substance in a given amount of liquid or air
senses.definitionCN: 一定量液体或空气中所含某物质的量
senses.example: The concentration of salt in the water is low.
senses.exampleCN: 水中盐的浓度很低。
senses.why: How much is packed into a space is the scientific face of the same word.
senses.whyCN: 一个空间里装了多少，是这个词的科学一面。

intro.en: Concentration comes from Latin com-, together, and centrum, centre, through the verb concentrare.
intro.cn: concentration 来自拉丁语 com-（一起）与 centrum（中心），经动词 concentrare 演变而来。

items.en: Centrum named the middle point of a circle.
items.cn: centrum 指圆的中心点。

items.en: Concentrare meant to bring things to one centre.
items.cn: concentrare 意为把东西聚到一个中心。

items.en: French concentration named the act of gathering.
items.cn: 法语 concentration 指聚集的行为。

items.en: English concentration first meant the act of bringing to a centre.
items.cn: 英语 concentration 最初指聚到中心的行为。

items.en: Science gave it the sense of strength in a mixture.
items.cn: 科学又赋予它混合物中浓度的含义。

note.cn: 形近组收的是与 concentration 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示注意力与密度的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a spotlight on one point, then move to crowded places and to strong mixtures.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从打在一个点上的聚光灯开始，再走到拥挤的地方与浓的混合物。

normal.en: Concentration is what a spotlight does: one point, all the light.
normal.cn: concentration 就是聚光灯做的事：一个点，全部的光。

normal.en: The noun ends in -tion, so it names the state, not the act of trying.

normal.en: Lose concentration and the page turns back into marks.

normal.en: A high concentration of salt means a lot of salt in little water.
normal.cn: 盐的浓度高，就是少量水里有很多盐。

normal.en: Factories in one valley show a concentration of industry.
normal.cn: 工厂聚在一个山谷，显示出产业的集中。

abstract.en: Picture a single lamp lighting one small circle in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象黑屋里一盏灯只照亮一个小圆圈。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pressed into one narrow street.
abstract.cn: 想象人群挤进一条窄街。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon of syrup in a glass of water.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水里的一勺糖浆。

branches.cn: 化学衡量的是一个空间里装了多少。

branches.en: Mind and crowd both become stronger at one point.
branches.cn: 心思与人群都在一个点上变得更强。

branches.en: Gathering things and packing a liquid follow one pattern.
branches.cn: 聚拢东西与装浓液体遵循同一种模式。

intro.en: Concentration is built on Latin com-, together, plus centrum, centre, with the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: concentration 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、centrum（中心）与名词词尾 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The centre base centr- also gives central, eccentric and centrifugal.
latinIntro.cn: 中心词基 centr- 还给出 central、eccentric 与 centrifugal。

items.exampleCN: 样本显示出不同的浓度。
请把注意力放在问题上。

items.example: She sat concentrating for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 她坐着专注了一个小时。
安静有让人专注的力量。

items.example: The older text uses concentrical rings.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本用 concentrical 表示同心环。

definition_zh: 污垢；泥土；丑闻
definition_en: loose earth, dust or unwanted matter that makes something unclean
core_image: 指甲缝里嵌着一圈黑泥，用水冲也冲不干净
scene: 孩子从院子里跑进来，鞋底在地板上留下一串土印。 He washed the dirt off his hands.
sceneCN: 这里 dirt 指「污垢」（第 1 个义项：沾在东西上的脏物）；句意是他把手上的泥洗掉了。

derivatives.zh: 脏的；卑鄙的
肮脏
肮脏地

senses.title: Matter that makes things unclean
senses.definition: dust, mud or grease that spoils the surface it touches
senses.definitionCN: 落在表面上、把东西弄脏的灰、泥或油污
senses.example: He washed the dirt off his hands.
senses.exampleCN: 他把手上的泥洗掉了。
senses.why: You can see where it has been, even after it is gone.
senses.whyCN: 就算它被洗掉了，你仍看得出它待过哪里。

senses.title: Loose earth on the ground
senses.definition: the soft brown material that covers the ground
senses.definitionCN: 铺在地面上的松软褐色物质
senses.example: The children played in the dirt behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在屋后的泥地里玩。
senses.why: The same word names the ground itself and the mark it leaves.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指地面本身，也指它留下的印子。

senses.title: Hidden scandal about a person
senses.definition: unpleasant private information that can harm someone's name
senses.definitionCN: 能损害某人名声的难堪私事
senses.example: The paper paid a lot for dirt on the mayor.
senses.exampleCN: 那家报纸花了不少钱买市长的把柄。
senses.why: A stain on a name works like a stain on cloth.
senses.whyCN: 名字上的污点，和布上的污点一样难洗。

intro.en: Dirt came from Old Norse drit, a word for filth, and pushed aside the older English terms for mud and waste.
intro.cn: dirt 来自古诺斯语 drit（污秽），挤掉了英语原有的几个说法。

items.en: A root drit- named filth and waste matter.
items.cn: 词根 drit- 指污秽与排泄物。

items.en: Drit meant excrement or any filthy substance.
items.cn: drit 指排泄物或任何污秽之物。

items.en: Drit and dirt named mud, dung and waste on the ground.
items.cn: drit 与 dirt 指地上的泥、粪与脏东西。

items.en: Dirt widened to include loose earth as well as filth.
items.cn: dirt 的用法扩大，既指污秽也指松散的泥土。

items.en: The word now covers dust, mud and hidden scandal alike.
items.cn: 如今这个词兼指灰尘、泥土与见不得光的丑事。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single sound, while the meaning group names kinds of earth and waste.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个音，近义组则区分几种土与脏物。

entries.definition: to move quickly and suddenly
entries.definitionCN: 飞快地突然移动

entries.definition: force or effort, used in the phrase by dint of
entries.definitionCN: 力量或努力，见于 by dint of 一语

entries.definition: a long dagger once carried in Scotland
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰人从前佩带的长匕首

entries.definition: the upper layer of earth in which plants grow
entries.definitionCN: 植物生长的表层土壤

entries.definition: wet earth that sticks to shoes and clothes
entries.definitionCN: 粘在鞋和衣服上的湿泥

entries.definition: fine dry powder that settles on surfaces
entries.definitionCN: 落在表面的细干粉末

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from mud on a shoe to a stain that cannot be washed off a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从鞋上的泥，走到名字上洗不掉的污点。

normal.en: Dirt is short and ugly, like the mark it leaves.
normal.cn: dirt 这个词又短又硬，像它留下的那道印子。

normal.en: Dirt makes a clean thing show where it has been.
normal.cn: 干净的东西一沾上污垢，就显出它待过哪里。

normal.en: A dirt road is named for what it is made of.
normal.cn: 土路就是以它所用的材料命名的。

normal.en: Dirt cheap means the price is as low as the ground.
normal.cn: dirt cheap 是说价钱低到贴着地面。

normal.en: Dirt on a person is a stain that water cannot reach.
normal.cn: 一个人身上的 dirt，是一盆水洗不到的污点。

abstract.en: Picture a thumb pressed into soft brown earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一根拇指按进松软的褐色泥土。

abstract.en: Picture a white cloth with one dark fingerprint.
abstract.cn: 想象一块白布上有一个深色指印。

abstract.en: Picture a page of gossip folded small and hidden.
abstract.cn: 想象一页闲话被折小、藏了起来。

examples.en: There was dirt under every fingernail.
examples.cn: 每片指甲底下都是泥。

examples.en: The bike threw dirt onto the clean floor.
examples.cn: 自行车把泥甩到了干净的地板上。

examples.en: They built the hut on a dirt floor.
examples.cn: 他们把棚屋盖在泥地上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dirt 记成「得特脏」：这东西一沾身，就得特意去洗一遍。

root: 来自古诺斯语 drit，指污秽与排泄物，与古英语中几个表示泥污的词竞争后胜出。十六世纪起，词义从污秽扩展到松散的泥土；后来又引申为一个人见不得光的丑事，像名字上的一块污迹。

sensesIntro.en: From the mark on a hand, to the earth under a hut, to the scandal that stains a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手上的泥印，到棚屋下的泥地，再到玷污名声的丑事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark mark left where a clean surface was touched.
core.cn: 核心意象：干净表面被碰过之后留下的深色印子。

chain: EARTH LIES LOOSE ON THE GROUND
A ROAD IS PACKED FROM IT
SECRETS ARE DUG UP LIKE IT

branches.en: The first sense is the filth that spoils a surface.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是弄脏表面的污物。

branches.en: The second sense is the earth itself, loose underfoot.
branches.cn: 第二个义项就是脚下的松土。

branches.en: The third sense turns the stain into a hidden story.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把污迹变成一段藏起来的往事。

branches.en: The ground and the mark it leaves share one name.
branches.cn: 泥土与它留下的印子共用一个名字。

branches.en: Both kinds of dirt are hard to remove once seen.
branches.cn: 两种 dirt 一旦被看见，都很难洗掉。

intro.en: Dirt is a short base that builds a small family of adjectives, adverbs and compounds.
intro.cn: dirt 是个短词基，带出一小族形容词、副词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word came from Old Norse and grows with English endings.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；这个词出自古诺斯语，靠英语词尾生长。

items.example: The dirt came off with warm water.
His shoes were dirty after the walk.
items.exampleCN: 走完那段路他的鞋脏了。

items.example: The dirtiness of the room shocked her.
Only a dirtbag would cheat a child.

items.meaning: a light motorcycle made for rough ground
items.example: He rode a dirt bike along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 他骑着越野摩托沿山脊走。

items.meaning: a road made of packed earth
items.example: The dirt road turned to mud in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 一下雨土路就变成了泥。

items.example: The old chairs were dirt cheap.
items.exampleCN: 那些旧椅子便宜得离谱。

definition_zh: 版本；说法、描述；（软件、文件的）修订本；改编本
definition_en: a particular form of something that differs from other forms of it, such as a copy, an account, or an edition
core_image: 同一份稿子被改了又改，桌上摊着好几份，每一份都略有不同
scene: 编辑把同一篇文章的三个版本并排打开，逐段比较。 The final version was shorter than the first one by two pages.
sceneCN: 这里 version 是「版本」（第 1 个义项：与同一事物的其他形式不同的某个形态）；句意为最终版本比第一版短了两页。几份稿子并排放在桌上，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：版本；说法；改编本；译文

collocations.phrase: a film version of the novel

derivatives.zh: 加形容词后缀构成，义为「与版本有关的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「版本管理、版本化」
同一拉丁词根 vert-「转」构成，义为「多才多艺的；多用途的」
同一词根构成，义为「转换；改变信仰」

senses.title: One form among many
senses.titleCN: 版本：众多形态中的一种
senses.definition: a particular form of something, in which it differs from other forms of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的一种特定形态，与其他形态有所差别
senses.example: The paper published a longer version of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了那次访谈的较长版本。
senses.why: Latin vertere means to turn; a version is the same matter turned a little differently.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertere 意为「转」；version 就是同一件事被稍稍转了个角度。

senses.title: One person's account
senses.titleCN: 说法：某人对事情的一种讲法
senses.definition: one person's account of an event, especially when others may tell it differently
senses.definitionCN: 某人对一件事的讲述，尤指他人可能有不同讲法时
senses.example: The two witnesses gave very different versions of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人对事故的说法大相径庭。
senses.why: An account is also a turning: the same event passes through one perspective and comes out shaped by it.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是一种转动：同一件事经过一个人的视角，出来时已被这个视角塑形。

senses.title: An edition or revision
senses.titleCN: 修订本：经过修改的一版
senses.definition: a revised or updated edition of a text, file or product
senses.definitionCN: 文本、文件或产品经过修改更新的一个版本
senses.example: This is the third version of the manual, and it is much clearer.
senses.exampleCN: 这是手册的第三版，清楚多了。
senses.why: Each revision turns the draft once more, and the newest turn is what users install.
senses.whyCN: 每一次修订都把稿子再转一次，最新的那一转就是用户安装的那个。

senses.title: An adaptation
senses.titleCN: 改编本：由原作改成的形式
senses.definition: a form of a work that has been adapted for another medium or audience
senses.definitionCN: 为另一种媒介或受众改编而成的作品形式
senses.example: The film version leaves out the youngest brother entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 电影改编版把最小的弟弟整个删掉了。
senses.why: Moving a story to the screen is a literal turning: the same characters now seen from a new side.
senses.whyCN: 把故事搬上银幕是一种字面意义上的转动：同一些人物从新的方向被看见。

senses.title: A specific release of software
senses.titleCN: 软件的一个具体发行版
senses.definition: a numbered release of a program or document, used to track changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 带编号的程序或文档发行版本，用于追踪变化
senses.example: Please update to version 4.2 before sending the file.
senses.exampleCN: 发送文件之前请更新到 4.2 版。
senses.why: In modern use the turning is numbered: each fix produces one more version on the record.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法里，这种转动被编了号：每修一处，记录上就多一个版本。

intro.en: Version comes from the Latin verb 'to turn', and the whole family follows that image of turning.
intro.cn: version 源自拉丁语表示「转」的动词，整个词族都沿着这一转动的意象展开。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn, turn around, change'; it lies behind convert, revert and reverse.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转、回转、改变」，它是 convert、revert、reverse 背后的词。

items.en: Versio meant 'a turning, a change, a translation'; the noun names the act of turning something.
items.cn: versio 意为「转动、改变、翻译」，这一名词指把某物转一次这件事。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word for a translation or rendering of a text.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个词，指文本的翻译或转写。

items.en: English adopted version first for translations, then for any form differing from another.
items.cn: 英语最初用 version 指译本，后来泛指与其他形式有别的任一形态。

items.en: Publishing, then computing, turned it into a counting word: first version, final version, version number.
items.cn: 出版业再到计算机业把它变成计数词：第一版、最终版、版本号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin turn-root; the near-meaning group gathers words for forms and accounts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「转」词根构成的词；近义组收表示形态与说法的词。

entries.definition: The act of turning something into another form or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转换、转变」，指把某物变成另一形态或用途。

entries.definition: To turn the other way round; the opposite direction of the same turn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「颠倒、反转」，是同一转动的相反方向。

entries.definition: Turned apart, hence different; a family voice of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，本义为「转向不同方向」。

entries.definition: Able to turn to many uses or skills.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多才多艺的、多用途的」，即能转向许多用途。

entries.definition: One printing or published form of a text, usually revised.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版次」，指文本的一次印行，通常经过修订。

entries.definition: A report or description of what happened; the everyday word for sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、说法」，是义项 02 的日常词。

entries.definition: A form that differs slightly, often in spelling or wording.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体」，指略有差别的形式，多指拼写或措辞。

entries.definition: A performance or translation of a work, stressing the performer's version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演绎、译文」，强调表演者或译者的处理。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb vertere and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 vertere，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: version shares its root with turn: each version is the same thing turned again.
normal.cn: version 与 turn 同根：每个版本都是同一件东西又转过一次。

normal.en: Different witnesses, different versions: the same event turned through different eyes.
normal.cn: 不同的证人给出不同的说法：同一件事经过不同的眼睛转动一次。

normal.en: Software asks for a version number; a novel asks for a film version.
normal.cn: 软件要的是版本号；小说要的是电影改编版。

normal.en: The original version stays the reference while later versions move away from it.
normal.cn: 原版始终是参照，后来的版本则离它越来越远。

normal.en: Ver- inside version echoes vertere, the turning verb of Latin.
normal.cn: version 里的 ver- 呼应 vertere，即拉丁语那个「转」的动词。

abstract.en: Picture one sheet of paper on a turntable: each small rotation shows a slightly different face, and each face is a version.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸放在转盘上：每一次微转都露出略不同的正面，每一面都是一个版本。

abstract.en: A version is never the thing itself, only a way of seeing it, which is why accounts can disagree.
abstract.cn: 版本从来不是事物本身，只是一种看它的方式，所以各种说法可以彼此矛盾。

abstract.en: The word travels from clay tablets to code without changing its logic: turn, compare, number.
abstract.cn: 这个词从泥板一路走到代码，逻辑却没变：转动、比较、编号。

examples.en: This is an older version of the map, without the new road.
examples.cn: 这是这幅地图的旧版本，上面还没有那条新路。

examples.en: Each witness told a slightly different version of the night.
examples.cn: 每个证人对那一夜的讲述都略有不同。

examples.en: The app will not open until you install the latest version.
examples.cn: 不安装最新版本，这个应用就打不开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）想（sion）」——同一个故事，我想的说法和别人不一样：版本

root: 源自拉丁语 versio「转动、翻译」，来自动词 vertere「转」；经古法语进入英语；同族词有 convert、reverse、diverse、versatile。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of version all rest on one turning: the same matter presented in another form, as an account, an edition, an adaptation, or a numbered release.
sensesIntro.cn: version 的五个义项都建立在一次转之上：同一件事以另一种形态出现，或是说法、或是修订本、或是改编、或是编号发行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheets of one article side by side on a desk, each slightly changed.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一篇文章的几份稿子并排在桌上，每份都略有变化。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the noun names any one form of many.
branches.cn: 形态线：名词指众多形态中的任意一种。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: an account is the event turned through one person.
branches.cn: 说法线：说法就是事件经过某个人转动后的样子。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: editions and software releases are numbered turns.
branches.cn: 计数线：版本与软件发行都是被编号的一次转动。

branches.en: MEDIUM LINE: the story turns from page to screen.
branches.cn: 媒介线：故事从纸面转到银幕。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the original is the point from which every version departs.
branches.cn: 对照线：原版是所有版本由之离开的那个点。

intro.en: Version is a Latin noun stem with an English noun ending; the turning root stays visible inside it.
intro.cn: version 是拉丁语名词词干加英语名词词尾，其中的「转」词根仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vertere, with the noun versio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：动词 vertere 及其名词 versio。

items.example: It forms version from the stem.

definition_zh: 侧面轮廓；侧影；人物简介；概况资料；作简介
definition_en: the outline of a face or object seen from the side, a short description of someone, or a set of recorded characteristics
core_image: 光从一侧打来，人脸的外缘被描成一条清楚的线，线内是暗的，线外是亮的
scene: 他侧身站在窗前，光从一边照过来，额头、鼻梁和下巴的边沿被勾成一条清楚的线。 In the photograph she was shown in profile, her chin slightly raised.
sceneCN: 这里表示「侧面轮廓」（第 1 个义项：从侧面看到的头部或物体外缘线条）；句意为照片里她以侧面示人，下巴微微抬起。

pos.zh: 侧面轮廓；侧影；简介；概况资料

derivatives.zh: 由 profile 加 -ing 构成，义为「资料分析；人物画像」
由 profile 加 -er 构成，义为「做资料分析、绘制画像的人」
由 profile 加 -ed 构成，义为「被写成简介的；被勾勒出轮廓的」

senses.title: The outline of a head seen from the side
senses.definition: the shape of a person's head or face as seen from one side
senses.definitionCN: 从一侧看到的人头或面部的形状
senses.example: Her profile was drawn in a single line.
senses.exampleCN: 她的侧影被一笔勾成。
senses.why: Italian profilo came from a verb meaning to draw in outline, and the first thing so drawn was the edge of a face against the light.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 profilo 出自意为「勾轮廓」的动词，最早被这样勾出的就是逆光中脸的边缘。

senses.title: A short written description of a person or place
senses.definition: a short article or account that describes someone's life, work or character
senses.definitionCN: 简要描述某人生活、工作或性格的文章或叙述
senses.example: The magazine ran a profile of the young architect.
senses.exampleCN: 杂志刊登了一篇这位年轻建筑师的简介。
senses.why: An outline leaves out the interior and keeps only the edge; in the same way a profile sketches the main facts and leaves the rest unstated.
senses.whyCN: 轮廓只留边缘、略去内部；同样，人物简介只勾主要事实，其余留白。

senses.title: A set of recorded characteristics about someone or something
senses.definition: a collection of information about a person, group or thing, used to classify or analyse them
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人、某群体或某事物的信息集合，用于分类或分析
senses.example: The company builds a profile of each customer.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为每位顾客建立一份资料档案。
senses.why: From a drawn edge the word moved to a data edge: the few recorded features that make a person or group identifiable.
senses.whyCN: 词义从「画出的边缘」转到「数据的边缘」：少数被记录下来的特征，足以把一个人或群体辨认出来。

senses.title: To describe someone or something in a short account
senses.definition: to write or broadcast a short account of a person, place or organisation
senses.definitionCN: 用短文或节目简要介绍某人、某地或某机构
senses.example: The paper profiled three local teachers last week.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸上周介绍了三位本地教师。
senses.why: If a profile is an outline in words, then to profile is simply to draw that outline, which is why the verb arrived later and keeps the same image.
senses.whyCN: 如果 profile 是用文字画的轮廓，那么 to profile 就是把这个轮廓画出来；动词出现较晚，却沿用同一幅画面。

intro.en: Profile reached English through Italian art and printing, where a line drawn round a head gave the word its name; the Latin element inside is filum, a thread.
intro.cn: profile 经意大利语的绘画与印刷用语进入英语，原指名绕头部画出的那条线；其中拉丁成分是 filum，意为「线、细丝」。

items.en: Filum meant a thread or a fine line, the material from which an outline could be imagined as spun.
items.cn: filum 意为线、细丝，轮廓正可以被想象成用这样的线绕出来的。

items.en: Filare meant to spin or to draw out into thread, and it supplied the verb behind the Italian word.
items.cn: filare 意为纺线、拉成丝，是意大利语那个动词的来源。

items.en: Italian profilare meant to draw in outline, especially the edge of a face or figure; it is generally taken as pro- plus filum.
items.cn: 意大利语 profilare 意为勾出轮廓，尤指脸或人体的外缘；一般认为它由 pro- 加 filum 构成。

items.en: The noun profilo was such an outline, and artists and engravers carried the term across Europe.
items.cn: 名词 profilo 就指这样一条轮廓线，画家与版画家把它带到了欧洲各地。

items.en: French took it as profil and English as profile; English later widened it from a drawn edge to a written sketch and then to a set of data.
items.cn: 法语作 profil，英语作 profile；英语后来从画出的边缘扩展到文字速写，再扩展到一组数据。

note.en: The first group collects words that only look or sound close, with unrelated origins; the second collects words for outlines and short descriptions.
note.cn: 第一组收只是拼写或读音相近、词源无关的词；第二组收表示轮廓与简短描述的词。

entries.definition: A folder or set of documents; the spelling is close but the origin is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 文件夹或一组文件；拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: Money gained in business; only the opening letters match.
entries.definitionCN: 经商所得的利润；只是开头几个字母相同。

entries.definition: Very deep or intense; the shared pro- is not a shared root.
entries.definitionCN: 极深的；强烈的；共有的 pro- 并不等于同根。

entries.definition: To declare openly; it shares the prefix but comes from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 公开声明；与本词共用前缀，却出自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The line that marks the outer edge of a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 标出形状外缘的线条。

entries.definition: A picture of a person, usually showing the face.
entries.definitionCN: 人物画像，通常以面部为主。

entries.definition: A quick rough drawing or a short account.
entries.definitionCN: 快速的粗略画稿或简短叙述。

entries.definition: The written life story of one person.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人一生的书面传记。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a thread drawn along the edge of a face, and every later sense keeps that idea of a line that marks only the outside.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是沿脸缘拉出的一条线，后来每个义项都保留着「只勾外部的一条线」这个想法。

normal.en: Filum is Latin for thread; think of a thread laid along the edge of a face to trace its outline.
normal.cn: filum 是拉丁语的「线」；想象把一根线贴着脸的边缘，把轮廓描出来。

normal.en: Italian profilo was an outline drawing, and English kept the picture when it borrowed the word.
normal.cn: 意大利语 profilo 就是轮廓画，英语借词时把这幅画一起借了过来。

normal.en: In profile means seen from the side, exactly the view in which an outline is clearest.
normal.cn: in profile 意为从侧面看，正是轮廓最清楚的那个角度。

normal.en: A written profile is an outline in words, which is why one word serves a face and a person's life.
normal.cn: 文字简介是用词句画的轮廓，所以同一个词既能用于脸，也能用于一个人的生平。

normal.en: Keep a low profile uses the same image: stay flat against the background, like a line that does not stand out.
normal.cn: keep a low profile 沿用同一幅画面：贴着背景伏低，像一条不显眼的线。

abstract.en: A profile is always a reduction: it keeps the edge and drops the depth, and that is exactly why it is useful.
abstract.cn: 轮廓永远是一种删减：留下边缘、舍去纵深，而这正是它有用的原因。

abstract.en: The move from a drawn face to a data record suggests that identity itself can be reduced to a few marked features.
abstract.cn: 从画出的脸到数据档案，这一步暗示身份本身也能被压缩成几个被标记的特征。

abstract.en: To be profiled is to be summarised by someone else, which is why the word can feel neutral in art and uneasy in policing.
abstract.cn: 被写进简介就是被别人概括，所以这个词在艺术里显得中性，在执法语境里却让人不安。

examples.en: He sat in profile against the bright window.
examples.cn: 他侧身坐着，背后是明亮的窗。

examples.en: The report includes a short profile of each candidate.
examples.cn: 报告为每位候选人附了一份简短介绍。

examples.en: She was profiled in a weekend magazine.
examples.cn: 一家周末杂志为她写了人物简介。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若费尔」——像用一根细线沿着脸边慢慢铺过去，费点功夫才勾得准；记住 profile 是侧面轮廓。

root: 一般认为来自意大利语 profilo（轮廓），由 profilare（勾轮廓）而来，可追溯到拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ filum（线、细丝），十七世纪进入英语；与 cedere、fateri 无关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a line tracing an outer edge; from it come the side view, the written sketch, the recorded set of features, and the verb that produces such a sketch.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是描出外缘的一条线；由此分出侧面像、文字速写、被记录的一组特征，以及制作这种速写的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine line running along the edge of a face lit from one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条细线沿着一侧受光的面部边缘游走。

branches.en: a face outlined by light from one side
branches.cn: 一侧的光把脸勾成轮廓

branches.en: a line drawn round a head, then a set of facts round a person
branches.cn: 先绕头画一条线，再绕一个人收集一组事实

branches.en: a magazine page sketching a life in a few hundred words
branches.cn: 杂志用几百字勾出一个人一生

branches.en: a table of recorded habits and preferences
branches.cn: 记录习惯与偏好的表格

branches.en: a journalist turning facts into a short portrait
branches.cn: 记者把事实写成一篇短小的人物速写

intro.en: A Latin word for thread, the verb of spinning it, and the Italian pair that turned it into an outline, plus English endings, hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「线」的拉丁词、纺线的动词、把它变成轮廓的意大利语一对词，再加英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to spin, to draw into thread

items.meaningCN: 做资料分析、绘制画像的人

latinEntries.meaning: to spin, to draw into thread

definition_zh: 拥有；所有物；属地；控球权
definition_en: the state of owning something, the things owned, territory held, or control of the ball in a game
core_image: 腰上挂着一串钥匙，走一步响一声
scene: 搬家那天箱子一只只打开，主人把每件旧物都擦了又擦。 Her possessions filled three rooms of the new flat.
sceneCN: 这里 possession 是「所有物」（第 2 个义项：属于某人的东西）；句意为她的物品装满了新公寓的三个房间。画面里有搬家的纸箱和擦拭旧物的手。

pos.zh: 拥有；所有物；属地；控球权

derivatives.zh: dis-（剥夺）加 possess 构成，义为「剥夺……的财产或土地」
同一词干加 -ive，义为「占有欲强的；所有格的」
同一词干加表示人的 -or，义为「拥有者；持有人」

senses.title: The state of owning something
senses.definition: the state of having something as your own, especially when this is recognized by law
senses.definitionCN: 把某物作为自己所有的状态，尤指得到法律承认的持有
senses.example: The house has been in the family's possession for a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子由这个家族持有一个世纪了。
senses.why: The Latin noun named the act of holding before it named the object, so the abstract state comes first in English too.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词先指持有的行为，后指被持有的物件，所以英语里抽象的「持有状态」也排在前面。

senses.title: Something that you own
senses.definition: a thing that belongs to you, usually used in the plural for someone's personal belongings
senses.definitionCN: 属于你的东西，通常用复数指某人的个人财物
senses.example: She packed her few possessions into one bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己不多的几件东西装进一个袋子。
senses.why: From the state of holding, the word slides to the things held; the plural then becomes the usual way to list them one by one.
senses.whyCN: 从持有的状态滑向被持有的东西，复数形式随后成了把这些东西一件件清点出来的常用说法。

senses.title: Land or territory held by a country
senses.definition: a country or region controlled by another country, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 受另一国控制的国或地区，常用复数
senses.example: The empire's overseas possessions were costly to defend.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国的海外属地防卫起来代价高昂。
senses.why: Since possidere pictured mastery over a place, the political sense of land held by force or treaty grew straight out of that picture.
senses.whyCN: 既然 possidere 的画面就是对一处地方的主宰，靠武力或条约占有的土地这一政治义便直接从那幅画面里长出来。

senses.title: Control of the ball in a sport
senses.definition: in team sports, the time during which one side has the ball and controls play
senses.definitionCN: 在团队运动中，一方持球并控制比赛节奏的那段时间
senses.example: The home side had possession for most of the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在下半场大部分时间里控制着球。
senses.why: Sport borrowed the legal idea of holding: the side that holds the ball holds the game, so possession names a temporary kind of control.
senses.whyCN: 体育借用了法律上的「持有」观念：持球的一方控制着比赛，于是 possession 用来指一种临时性的掌控。

intro.en: Possession is the noun built on the same Latin verb as possess, and it kept the whole range of that verb: holding, the thing held, and land held.
intro.cn: possession 是与 possess 同一个拉丁动词上的名词，完整保留了那个动词的范围：持有、被持有之物、被占有的土地。

items.en: Latin potis meant able or powerful, and it supplied the first element of the verb possidere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 potis 意为有能力的、有权的，它是动词 possidere 的前半部分。

items.en: Possidere combined potis with sedere, to sit, so that owning was pictured as sitting in command of a place.
items.cn: possidere 把 potis 与 sedere（坐）合成，于是拥有被想象成坐在一处地方发号施令。

items.en: The noun possessio covered the state of holding, the object held and land held, a range English took over almost whole.
items.cn: 名词 possessio 涵盖持有的状态、被持有的物件以及占有的土地，英语几乎整套接收了这一范围。

items.en: Anglo-Norman and Old French possession kept the same breadth, and legal French gave the word a firm place in English law.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-诺曼语与古法语的 possession 保留了同样的宽度，法律法语又让它在英国法中站稳了位置。

items.en: Modern English counts possessions in the plural for personal belongings, and uses the singular for territory and for control of the ball.
items.cn: 现代英语用复数 possessions 指个人财物，用单数指属地以及比赛中的控球权。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same holding family in its various forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for what a person owns.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个「持有」词族的不同词形；近义组收表示一个人所拥有之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to own or to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，意为拥有、持有。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person or grammar form that claims ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 形容占有欲强的人，或表示所属关系的语法形式。

entries.definition: To strip someone of property or land.
entries.definitionCN: 剥夺某人的财产或土地。

entries.definition: The one who holds what the noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 持有这个名词所指之物的人。

entries.definition: Things owned, especially land or buildings, and the right to them.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的东西，尤指土地房产及其权利。

entries.definition: The small personal things that someone carries or keeps.
entries.definitionCN: 某人随身携带或保存的个人小物件。

entries.definition: Something valuable that a person or company owns.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或公司拥有的有价值的东西。

normalIntro.en: The noun inherits a Latin verb about sitting as master, and its family spreads from a state of owning to the objects, the land, and even the ball.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词继承了一个「以主人身份坐定」的拉丁动词，词族从持有状态铺到物件、土地，甚至球。

normal.en: Potis meant able and sedere meant to sit, so the noun still carries the picture of a master seated over a place.
normal.cn: potis 意为有能力，sedere 意为坐，所以这个名词里仍坐着一位压住场子的主人。

normal.en: The suffix -ion turns the verb into the name of a state, so possession is the holding and not the holder.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ion 把动词变成状态的名字，所以 possession 是持有本身，而不是持有者。

normal.en: The plural possessions is the everyday word for the things scattered through your bags and rooms.
normal.cn: 复数 possessions 是日常说法，指散落在包里和房间里的那些东西。

normal.en: Dispossess adds dis-, away, and reverses the holding: the things are taken out of your hands.
normal.cn: dispossess 加上表示「离开」的 dis-，把持有反过来：东西被从你手里拿走。

normal.en: Legal English keeps possession for land and goods, which is why the word sounds formal in a courtroom.
normal.cn: 法律英语用 possession 指土地与货物，所以这个词在法庭上听起来很正式。

abstract.en: A ring of keys at the waist: each key is a possession, and the ring itself is possession.
abstract.cn: 腰间一串钥匙：每一把是一个所有物，而整串就是「拥有」本身。

abstract.en: Owning is a relation, not a thing, so one word can name both the state and the objects that fill it.
abstract.cn: 拥有是一种关系而不是一件东西，所以同一个词既能指状态，也能指填满这个状态的那些物件。

abstract.en: When a country calls a distant island a possession, the word quietly turns land and people into property.
abstract.cn: 当一个国家把远方岛屿称作 possession，这个词就悄悄把土地和人变成了财产。

examples.en: The old house came into her possession last spring.
examples.cn: 这栋老房子去年春天归她所有。

examples.en: He lost most of his possessions in the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水让他失去了大部分财物。

examples.en: The team kept possession and waited for an opening.
examples.cn: 球队保持控球，等待机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怕塞身」——家当太多，全塞在身上就走不动；记住 possession 是财物。

root: 与 possess 同源，出自拉丁动词 possidere（占有）的名词形式 possessio，词干 possess- 加 -ion；同族词围绕「持有者、被持有物、剥夺」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the state of holding; from it come the things held, the land a country holds, and the temporary holding of a ball.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是持有这一状态；由此分出被持有的东西、一国所占的土地，以及比赛里对球的临时持有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of keys at the waist that sounds with every step.
core.cn: 核心意象：腰间一串钥匙，每走一步就响一声。

branches.en: a deed that proves who may stay
branches.cn: 证明谁有权住下的地契

branches.en: a bag of worn clothes in a doorway
branches.cn: 门口一袋穿旧的衣服

branches.en: an island drawn in one colour on a map
branches.cn: 地图上被涂成一种颜色的岛

branches.en: ten seconds of passing before a shot
branches.cn: 出手前十秒的传导

branches.en: a watch kept for years and worn every day
branches.cn: 珍藏多年、天天佩戴的表

intro.en: The word is the noun of state from a Latin verb of mastery, and its endings mark a person, a tendency, and a reversal.
intro.cn: 这个词是那个表示主宰的拉丁动词的状态名词，它的词尾分别标出人、倾向和反转。

latinIntro.en: The noun rests on a recorded Latin verb and its noun possessio, with potis and sedere as the two elements inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个名词依托有记录的拉丁动词及其名词 possessio，内部两个成分是 potis 与 sedere。

definition_zh: 停止；放弃；辞职；离开；退出
definition_en: to stop doing something; to leave a job; to leave a place, in a formal older use; to close a computer program
core_image: 一张被清空的办公桌，工牌孤零零放在桌角
scene: 办公室的抽屉被清空，工牌放在桌上，她向同事点了最后一次头。 After ten years she decided to quit her job and open a small bookshop.
sceneCN: 这里 quit 是「辞职、离开工作岗位」（第 2 个义项：主动离开一份工作）；句意为干了十年之后，她决定辞掉工作去开一家小书店。画面里可留意：清空的抽屉、桌上的工牌、最后一次点头。

pos.zh: 停止；放弃；辞职；离开；退出
已摆脱的；自由的（旧用法）

derivatives.zh: quit 加 -er，指轻易放弃的人
与 quit 同族的旧法律词，指债务的清偿或免除证明
re- 加同源词，指回报、酬谢或报复

senses.title: To stop doing something
senses.definition: to stop doing an activity, especially a habit
senses.definitionCN: 停止进行某项活动，尤指戒除习惯
senses.example: He quit smoking last year.
senses.exampleCN: 他去年戒了烟。
senses.why: Old French quiter meant to set free or release, and releasing a habit is the modern everyday sense of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 quiter 意为释放、解除，而把一个习惯「释放掉」正是这个动词今天最日常的用法。

senses.title: To leave a job
senses.definition: to leave a job or position, usually by your own choice
senses.definitionCN: 离开一份工作或职位，通常是主动选择
senses.example: She quit her job to travel for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 她辞了工作去旅行一年。
senses.why: If a job is a bond that holds you, quitting is leaving that bond behind, and the word came to mean resigning.
senses.whyCN: 工作像一条系住你的纽带，quit 就是离开这条纽带，于是这个词引申为辞职。

senses.title: To leave a place
senses.definition: to depart from a place, a formal or old-fashioned use
senses.definitionCN: 从某地离开，属正式或旧时用法
senses.example: The guests quit the hall before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 客人们在午夜前离开了大厅。
senses.why: The older sense of being released from a place produced the neutral meaning of simply departing from it.
senses.whyCN: 「从某地获释」这一较早的意思，生出「单纯离开某地」这一中性含义。

senses.title: To close a program
senses.definition: to close a computer program or application
senses.definitionCN: 关闭一个计算机程序或应用
senses.example: Quit the app before you restart the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 重启机器前先退出这个应用。
senses.why: Computing borrowed a firm everyday verb for ending an activity, because a program must be told clearly to stop.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了这个表示「结束活动」的干脆动词，因为程序需要被明确告知停止。

intro.en: Quit came from a French verb meaning to set free, which rested on the Latin word for rest; the path from released to stopped explains its senses.
intro.cn: quit 来自一个意为「释放」的法语动词，其根基是拉丁语表示休息的词；从「被释放」到「停止」这条路径解释了它的各个义项。

items.en: Quies meant rest, and the related verb meant to bring someone or something to rest.
items.cn: quies 意为休息，相关的动词意为使某人或某物安歇下来。

items.en: Quietus meant freed from a duty or a debt, released from an obligation.
items.cn: quietus 意为从义务或债务中解脱，被免除了责任。

items.en: Quiter meant to release, to acquit, and also to leave a place.
items.cn: quiter 意为释放、免除，也指离开某地。

items.en: Middle English quit meant to pay off, to set free, and later to give up an activity.
items.cn: 中古英语的 quit 意为清偿、使自由，后来指放弃一项活动。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb for stopping habits, for resigning, for leaving and for closing a program.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个动词指戒除习惯、辞职、离开以及关闭程序。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the root and its near homophone; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of stopping, leaving and resigning.
note.cn: 形近组收该词根的形式与近音词；近义组收表示停止、离开与辞职的动词。

entries.definition: To a great degree or completely.
entries.definitionCN: 相当地或完全地，与 quit 拼写相近但词义不同。

entries.definition: Making little noise and staying calm.
entries.definitionCN: 声音小且保持平静。

entries.definition: A person who gives up too easily.
entries.definitionCN: 轻易放弃的人。

entries.definition: To return a favour or a wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 回报恩惠或报复伤害。

entries.definition: To end an action or a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 结束一个动作或运动。

entries.definition: To leave a job formally.
entries.definitionCN: 正式辞去工作。

entries.definition: To give up something completely.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底放弃某事物。

entries.definition: To go away from a place or a person.
entries.definitionCN: 离开一个地方或一个人。

normalIntro.en: The word began as being set free from a duty, and giving up a habit or a job is a modern version of that release.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「从义务中获释」开始，而戒掉习惯或辞去工作正是这种解脱的现代版本。

normal.en: Quit and quiet share a Latin root, but one means to leave a duty while the other means to stay at rest.
normal.cn: quit 与 quiet 同出一个拉丁词根，但一个指离开义务，一个指留在安静里。

normal.en: Quit smoking is the pattern for habits: the verb takes a noun ending in -ing, not an infinitive.
normal.cn: quit smoking 是戒除习惯的固定搭配：动词后面接 -ing 形式，不接不定式。

normal.en: The past tense is quit, not quitted, in everyday modern English.
normal.cn: 现代日常英语里过去式是 quit，而不是 quitted。

normal.en: A quitter is someone who quits too soon, so the derived noun carries a judgement.
normal.cn: quitter 指过早放弃的人，这个派生名词自带评价。

normal.en: Quit the app means close it deliberately, not just leave it running in the background.
normal.cn: quit the app 指主动关闭程序，而不只是让它留在后台运行。

abstract.en: Quitting is usually described as failure, yet every change of direction requires leaving something behind.
abstract.cn: 放弃通常被说成失败，但每一次改变方向都需要把某些东西留在身后。

abstract.en: To quit a habit is to decide that the person you want to be matters more than the comfort you know.
abstract.cn: 戒掉一个习惯，就是认定你想成为的那个人比熟悉的舒适更重要。

abstract.en: The word releases you from an obligation, and only you can decide whether the release is escape or freedom.
abstract.cn: 这个词把你从义务中释放，而这份释放究竟是逃避还是自由，只有你能判定。

examples.en: He quit drinking after the doctor warned him.
examples.cn: 医生警告之后，他戒了酒。

examples.en: She quit her job and moved to a smaller town.
examples.cn: 她辞了工作，搬到一座小城。

examples.en: Do not quit the program while it is saving the file.
examples.cn: 程序正在保存文件时不要退出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「快特」——干脆利落地转身就走，记住 quit 是停止、辞职。

root: 拉丁语 quies（休息）→ quietus（获释的）→ 古法语 quiter（释放、离开）→ 英语 quit；同族有 quiet、quitter、requite。

sensesIntro.en: The core is release from a bond; the senses divide into stopping a habit, resigning a post, leaving a place and closing a program.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「从束缚中解脱」；义项分为戒除习惯、辞去职位、离开场所与关闭程序。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cleared desk with a single staff card left at its corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张清空的办公桌，桌角只留下一张工牌。

branches.en: a packet of cigarettes left unopened
branches.cn: 一包没拆封的香烟

branches.en: a key handed back at a front desk
branches.cn: 在前台交还的一把钥匙

branches.en: a hall emptying before midnight
branches.cn: 午夜前空下来的大厅

branches.en: a screen returning to the desktop

branches.cn: 同一种解脱，一次用于习惯，一次用于工作

intro.en: The word comes from the Latin noun for rest and a French verb of release, with English endings that build agents and related verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语表示休息的名词与法语表示释放的动词，并加上构成施动者与相关动词的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root quiet- is shared with quiet, though the two English words have parted ways in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 quiet- 与 quiet 共用，但这两个英语词在意义上已经分家。

items.cn: 拼写固定为 fortnight。

items.cn: 它也开始表示两周假期。

abstract.en: A fortnight is two weeks holding hands.

abstract.en: British speech folds nights into time.

abstract.en: Fourteen days can change a whole life.
abstract.cn: 十四天可以改变一生。

core.en: Fourteen nights joined into one block of time.

definition_zh: 区分；辨认出；使杰出
definition_en: to see or explain the difference between things, or to make yourself noticed by doing well
core_image: 两片相似的叶子放在掌心，先看边缘的锯齿，再看叶脉
scene: 两片叶子几乎一样，他并排举到光下看了很久。 Can you distinguish the real note from the copy?
sceneCN: 这里 distinguish 指「区分」（第 1 个义项：看出两者的差别）；句意是你能分辨真钞和假钞吗。

senses.title: To tell two things apart
senses.definition: to see or explain how two things are different
senses.definitionCN: 看出或说明两样东西的不同
senses.example: Children must learn to distinguish fact from opinion.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子必须学会区分事实与看法。
senses.why: Two things only need telling apart when they look alike.
senses.whyCN: 只有长得像的东西，才需要去分辨。

senses.title: To make out with the senses
senses.definition: to manage to see, hear or recognize something faint
senses.definitionCN: 努力看清、听见或认出模糊的东西
senses.example: I could not distinguish her face in the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 在人群里我认不出她的脸。
senses.why: The eye does the same work as the mind, only faster.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛做的和脑子是同一件事，只是更快。

senses.title: To stand out by doing well
senses.definition: to make yourself noticed through good work
senses.definitionCN: 靠出色的表现让人注意到自己
senses.example: He distinguished himself in the final debate.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一场辩论中表现突出。
senses.why: One clear mark is enough to lift a name out of the list.
senses.whyCN: 一个清楚的记号，就足以让一个名字从名单里立起来。

intro.en: Distinguish comes from Latin distinguere, to separate by marking, from dis-, apart, and stinguere, to prick.
intro.cn: distinguish 来自拉丁语 distinguere（做记号分开），由 dis-（分开）与 stinguere（刺）构成。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or put a mark on something.
items.cn: stinguere 指刺一下或在东西上留记号。

items.en: Dis- carried the marked item away from its neighbours.
items.cn: dis- 把做过记号的那件从旁边的东西里分出来。

items.en: Distinguere grew to mean telling one thing from another.
items.cn: distinguere 逐渐表示把一物与另一物分辨开。

items.en: English used it for seeing a difference.
items.cn: 英语借入时表示看出差别。

items.en: The sense of standing out by merit appeared.
items.cn: 后来出现靠功绩出众的意思。

items.en: Today a good reader distinguishes tone as well as words.
items.cn: 今天好的读者既分辨字面，也分辨语气。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the marking stem, while the meaning group gathers other verbs of telling apart.
note.cn: 形近组共享「做记号」的词干，近义组则是几个表示分辨的动词。

entries.definition: clear and clearly separate
entries.definitionCN: 清楚而分明的

entries.definition: a difference, or high quality
entries.definitionCN: 差别，或卓越

entries.definition: able to be told apart
entries.definitionCN: 可区分的

entries.definition: to show or see a difference
entries.definitionCN: 显示或看出差别

entries.definition: to notice something faint or subtle
entries.definitionCN: 察觉微弱或细微之物

entries.definition: to name something correctly
entries.definitionCN: 正确认出并说出

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two leaves in one hand and end with a name lifted above the crowd.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从掌心里两片叶子开始，落到一个被举到人群之上的名字。

normal.en: Dis- plus stinguish: prick a mark, and the two come apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 stinguish，刺个记号，两者就分开了。

normal.en: A good cook can distinguish salt from sugar by touch.
normal.cn: 好厨子一摸就能分出盐和糖。

normal.en: At dusk you cannot distinguish the path from the grass.
normal.cn: 黄昏时你分不清小路和草地。

normal.en: She distinguished herself in the first round.
normal.cn: 她在第一轮就表现突出。

normal.en: Teachers distinguish effort from talent when they mark.
normal.cn: 老师批改时会区分努力与天赋。

abstract.en: Picture two leaves held up to the light, veins compared.
abstract.cn: 想象两片叶子举到光下比对叶脉。

abstract.en: Picture a mark pricked on one card among many.
abstract.cn: 想象许多卡片中有一张被刺了记号。

abstract.en: Picture one head rising above a seated crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象坐着的人群里有一个头抬得更高。

examples.en: It is hard to distinguish the two shades of blue.
examples.cn: 这两种蓝色很难分辨。

examples.en: She distinguished herself in the school choir.
examples.cn: 她在校合唱团里表现突出。

examples.en: He cannot distinguish left from right without a sign.
examples.cn: 没有标记他就分不清左右。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 distinguish 记成「刺个记号分出来」：dis 表示分开，stingu 来自刺，刺上记号，就能把相似的东西分辨开，做得好还会被单独看见。

root: 源自拉丁语 distinguere，由 dis-（分开）与 stinguere（刺）组成，本义是刺出记号把东西区别开。英语先指看出差别，再指在模糊中辨认出某物，后来引申为靠出色表现让自己被单独看见。

sensesIntro.en: From telling two leaves apart to making your own name stand out of the list.
sensesIntro.cn: 从分辨两片叶子，到让自己的名字从名单里立起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two look-alike leaves held to the light while the eyes compare their veins.
core.cn: 核心意象：两片相似的叶子举到光下，眼睛比对叶脉。

branches.en: The first sense is the work of telling two things apart.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把两样东西分辨开的工作。

branches.en: The second sense does that work with the senses alone.
branches.cn: 第二个义项只用五官来完成这件事。

branches.en: The third sense turns being noticed into being admired.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把被看见变成被称赞。

branches.en: Both senses need attention to a small difference.
branches.cn: 两个义项都需要留意细微的差别。

branches.en: Both senses depend on a mark that others can see.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖别人看得见的记号。

intro.en: Distinguish belongs to the marking family, where a pricked mark separates and also lifts a name.
intro.cn: distinguish 属于「做记号」一族，一道刺出的记号既能分开东西，也能让一个名字立起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin stinguere, to prick, gives distinguish and distinct; dis- turns one mark into a clear separation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stinguere（刺）给出 distinguish 与 distinct，前缀 dis- 把一个记号变成清楚的分隔。

items.example: Can you distinguish the two inks?

items.example: The distinction is easy to miss.
items.exampleCN: 这个区别很容易被忽略。

items.example: Her only distinguishing mark is a scar.
items.exampleCN: 她唯一可辨的标记是一道疤。

definition_zh: 缺口；间隙；差距；空白

core_image: 篱笆上露出一道能钻过狗的缺口
scene: 篱笆上有个缺口，狗钻了出去。 There is a gap in the fence where the dog got out.

senses.example: There is a gap in the fence where the dog got out.
senses.exampleCN: 篱笆上有个缺口，狗钻了出去。
senses.why: This is the physical opening sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是具体的开口义项。

senses.title: Break in time

senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的一段时间

senses.exampleCN: 两封信之间隔了两年。
senses.why: Space in time is pictured as a gap.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的空档被想象成缺口。

senses.title: Difference in amount
senses.definition: a difference between two amounts or levels
senses.definitionCN: 两个数量或水平之间的差异
senses.example: The gap between rich and poor is growing.
senses.exampleCN: 贫富差距正在扩大。
senses.why: Distance between figures feels like empty space.
senses.whyCN: 数字之间的距离像空档。

senses.title: Missing knowledge

senses.definitionCN: 知识或记录中缺失的部分

senses.exampleCN: 这份报告在叙述中留下了一处空白。
senses.why: Missing information is a gap in a whole.
senses.whyCN: 缺失的信息是整体中的缺口。

normalIntro.cn: gap 是物体、时间或数字中的空处。

normal.cn: 篱笆上有个缺口，狗钻了出去。

normal.en: There was a gap of two years between the letters.
normal.cn: 两封信之间隔了两年。

normal.en: The gap between rich and poor is growing.

abstract.cn: 缺口是新事物可以进入的地方。

abstract.cn: 照料上的小缝隙会变成信任上的大裂口。

senses.title: Eating less on purpose

senses.definitionCN: 为减轻体重而有意控制的一份饮食安排

senses.title: A constant supply of the same thing

intro.en: Diet goes back to Greek diaita, a way of living, and reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: diet 可追到希腊语 diaita（生活方式），经拉丁语和法语进入英语。

items.en: Diaita meant a way of life, including food, exercise and sleep.
items.cn: diaita 指一种生活方式，包含饮食、运动与睡眠。

items.en: Latin diaeta kept the medical sense of a regulated life.
items.cn: 拉丁语 diaeta 保留了「有节制的生活」这层医学含义。

items.en: Diete arrived in French as the food a sick person should take.
items.cn: 法语 diete 指病人该吃的东西。

items.en: English diet first named a fixed allowance of food and drink.
items.cn: 英语 diet 最初指定量配给的饮食。

items.en: It split into the daily fare of anyone and a plan to lose weight.
items.cn: 它分成两层：人人日常的吃食，以及减肥的计划。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of diet, while the meaning group covers food supply, cooking and nutrition.
note.cn: 形近组与 diet 读音相近，近义组则覆盖食物供给、烹饪与营养。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a plate of ordinary food and end with the word stretched to cover songs and jokes.

normal.en: Die with a t: die is what a strict diet tries to avoid.

normal.en: A diet is not a meal, it is the pattern behind many meals.

normal.en: Go on a diet means the plan starts today, not tomorrow.
normal.cn: go on a diet 意思是计划从今天起，不是明天。

normal.en: A balanced diet needs colour on the plate, not just weight on the scale.
normal.cn: 均衡饮食要盘里有颜色，不能只盯着秤上的数字。

normal.en: A diet of bad news is still a diet, though nothing is eaten.
normal.cn: 满耳朵坏消息也叫一种饮食，虽然什么也没吃。

abstract.en: Picture a plate divided into small coloured sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盘子被分成几块颜色不同的区域。

definition_zh: 假装；装作；声称；自称拥有；（游戏中）扮演；假装的
definition_en: to act as if something is true or real when it is not, or to claim a right or title for yourself
core_image: 一个人抬手在脸前撑起一块看不见的布，把表情挡在后面
scene: 午后的客厅里，孩子把几个靠垫围成一圈，说那是自己的城堡，母亲站在门边没有拆穿。 The boy liked to pretend that the cushions were the walls of a castle.
sceneCN: 这里 pretend 是「假装、装作」（第 1 个义项：明知不真，却演得像真的一样）；句意为男孩喜欢假装靠垫就是城堡的墙。图中可辨识物件：围成一圈的靠垫、客厅地毯、站在门边的母亲。

collocations.zh: 假装游戏（儿童想象性游戏）
