由 pretend 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「觊觎王位者；冒充者」
由 pretend 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「假装的；虚假的」

senses.title: To act as if something is true when it is not
senses.definition: to behave as if something is true or real while knowing that it is not
senses.definitionCN: 明知某事不真，却表现得像真的一样
senses.example: He pretended to be asleep when his mother opened the door.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲开门时，他假装睡着了。
senses.why: Latin praetendere meant to stretch something out in front of the body, and a made-up manner works exactly like that screen: it stands between you and the people looking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praetendere 本义是「把东西伸到身前」，而装出来的样子正像这样一块挡在身前的帘子，隔开自己和看过来的人，所以「假装」是这个动作最直接的用法。

senses.title: To claim a right or title for oneself
senses.definition: to put forward a claim to a right, title, or quality, often with little support
senses.definitionCN: 对某项权利、头衔或品质提出主张，常缺乏充分依据
senses.example: The young duke pretended to the throne after his uncle died.
senses.exampleCN: 叔父去世后，那位年轻的公爵声称王位应归自己。
senses.why: The oldest sense is holding something out in public and saying it is yours; a claim is that gesture performed with words instead of hands.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是把东西当众举起来、说它属于自己；所谓「声称拥有」，就是把这一动作改用言语来完成，手不必真的伸出去。

senses.title: To act out an imagined situation in play
senses.definition: to imagine that a scene is real and act it out, as children do in play
senses.definitionCN: 想象某个情境是真的并把它演出来，如儿童游戏中所为
senses.example: The children pretended that the sofa was a boat on the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把沙发当成一条船，假装在海上航行。
senses.why: Once the word means putting on a show, children's play becomes its natural home, because nothing in the scene has to be true for the scene to work.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词等于「演一场戏」，儿童游戏就成了它最自然的场所：布景不必为真，戏照样能演下去，所以「扮演」这一支从「假装」里长出来。

senses.title: Imaginary, used before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for something that exists only in play or in the imagination
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，形容只存在于游戏或想象中的事物
senses.example: Her daughter invented a pretend friend who lives under the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她女儿虚构了一个住在楼梯下的假想朋友。
senses.why: English often presses a verb into service as a modifier; a scene that is only performed needs a word to mark it as not real, and the bare verb does that job.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把动词直接拿来当修饰语；一段只在戏里存在的情境，需要一个词标明它并非真实，而光秃秃的动词正好担起这个差事，于是有了形容词用法。

intro.en: Pretend goes back to a Latin verb for stretching something out in front of you; the modern sense of a false show grew out of that gesture of holding a screen before the body.
intro.cn: pretend 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「把东西伸到身前」的动词；现代「假装」的义项，正是从「在身前撑起遮挡」这个动作长出来的。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front of, and it marks whatever is placed ahead of the body.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，标示被放到身体之前的东西。

items.en: The verb tendere meant to stretch or hold out, and it is the source of a large English family about stretching toward something.
items.cn: 动词 tendere 意为「伸展、伸出」，英语中一大族表示「朝某处伸展」的词都出自它。

items.en: Praetendere joined the two: to stretch something out in front, whether a cloak, an excuse, or a claim.
items.cn: praetendere 把两者合起来：把某物伸到前面，那可以是斗篷，也可以是借口或主张。

items.en: Old French pretendre meant to claim or assert, and English took that meaning over in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 pretendre 意为「声称、主张」，英语在十四世纪接受了这个意思。

items.en: From claiming something openly, the word slid toward claiming what is false, and later to children acting out a scene that never happened.
items.cn: 从公开声称某事，词义滑向声称不实之事，后来再指孩子在游戏里演出一段并未发生的情境。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for stretching; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs for putting on a false appearance.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「伸展」的动词展开；近义组收其他表示「装出假相」的动词。

entries.definition: A false claim or excuse, or the act of pretending.
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的声称或借口，也指假装这一行为。

entries.definition: A person who claims a title or position that is not theirs.
entries.definitionCN: 声称拥有不属于自己的头衔或地位的人；觊觎者。

entries.definition: A claim to importance or merit that is usually not deserved.
entries.definitionCN: 对重要性或优点的声称，通常并无资格。

entries.definition: A false reason given to hide the real one; it comes from a Latin verb meaning to weave, so it is only close in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 为掩盖真实原因而给出的假理由；它来自表示「编织」的拉丁动词，与本词只是拼写、读音接近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To make something false look real, or such a thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 让假的东西看起来像真的，也指这样的假货。

entries.definition: To pretend to have a feeling or an illness.
entries.definitionCN: 假装有某种感受或疾病；佯称。

entries.definition: To imitate the appearance or conditions of something.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿某物的外观或状况。

entries.definition: To pretend to be someone else, usually in order to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 假扮成别人，通常为了欺骗。

normalIntro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix of place and a verb of stretching, and its family keeps returning to what is held out in front of a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀和表示「伸展」的动词构成，同族词都围绕「伸到人前的东西」展开。

normal.en: Praetendere literally means to stretch something out in front, so the oldest picture is a screen held before the body.
normal.cn: praetendere 字面就是「把东西伸到前面」，最古老的画面是一块挡在身前的帘子。

normal.en: Tendere, the stretching verb, also gives extend, intend and tension, all of them about pulling or holding out.
normal.cn: 表示伸展的 tendere 还给出 extend、intend、tension，都跟拉长、伸出有关。

normal.en: Pretense is the noun of the same family: the false front itself rather than the act of putting it up.
normal.cn: pretense 是同一词族的名词，指那层假门面本身，而不是撑起门面的动作。

normal.en: Pretender keeps the older sense of claiming: a person who says a title belongs to them.
normal.cn: pretender 保留了「声称」的旧义：一个说某个头衔属于自己的人。

normal.en: The adjective pretend sits before a noun, as in pretend play, because it labels a whole scene rather than describing an action.
normal.cn: 作形容词的 pretend 站在名词前，如 pretend play，因为它标注的是一整段情境，而不是描述动作。

abstract.en: A screen in front of the body explains both branches: you hide behind it, and you also point to it as proof.
abstract.cn: 身前的帘子能解释两条分支：你躲在它后面，也指着它当凭证。

abstract.en: Pretending is not quite lying, because both sides may know the scene is invented.
abstract.cn: 假装不完全是说谎，因为双方可能都知道这场情境是编出来的。

abstract.en: Children do openly what adults do carefully: build a world, then live in it for an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 孩子把大人小心做的事公开做出来：搭起一个世界，然后整个下午住在里面。

examples.en: He pretended to be asleep when his mother opened the door.
examples.cn: 母亲开门时，他假装睡着了。

examples.en: The young duke pretended to the throne after his uncle died.
examples.cn: 叔父去世后，那位年轻的公爵声称王位应归自己。

examples.en: Her daughter invented a pretend friend who lives under the stairs.
examples.cn: 她女儿虚构了一个住在楼梯下的假想朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音近「扑来疼」——先扑到地上，再喊一声疼，整套动作都是装出来的。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ tendere（伸展）构成 praetendere，本义「伸到前面、举起示人」，经古法语 pretendre 进入英语；「举出主张」引申为「声称」，再引申为「假装」。注意 tendere 是「伸展」，与 prevent 所用的 venire（来）不同源，两词只共享前缀 prae-。

sensesIntro.en: The core gesture is holding something out in front of the body; the senses move from a public claim to a false show, then to play, then to the adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心动作是把东西举到身前；义项从公开的主张，走向虚假的展示，再走向游戏，最后是形容词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raising a screen between the face and the people watching.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在脸和旁观者之间举起一块遮挡物。

branches.en: a child closing his eyes and calling it sleep
branches.cn: 孩子闭上眼，说自己在睡觉

branches.en: cushions turned into castle walls
branches.cn: 靠垫被当成城堡的墙

branches.en: a nobleman pointing at a throne and naming it his
branches.cn: 贵族指着王座说那是自己的

branches.en: a sofa sailing across an imagined sea
branches.cn: 沙发在一片想象的海上航行

branches.en: a friend who lives under the stairs
branches.cn: 一个住在楼梯下的朋友

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix of place, a Latin verb of stretching, and the English endings that name the false front and the person who claims.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示位置的拉丁前缀、表示「伸展」的拉丁动词，以及命名假门面与声称者的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to stretch out in front, to put forward

latinEntries.meaning: to stretch out in front, to allege

definition_zh: 抗议；抗议活动；反对；申辩；坚称
definition_en: a public statement or action showing strong disagreement, the act of objecting in public, or a firm declaration that something is true
core_image: 一群人举着写满字的纸牌站在门前，谁都不肯散去
scene: 新规定贴出来的第二天清晨，居民们举着纸牌站到办公楼前，没有人愿意走开。 Hundreds of residents gathered outside the office to protest against the new rule.
sceneCN: 这里表示「抗议、反对」（第 2 个义项：公开表达强烈反对）；句意为数百名居民聚在办公楼外，抗议这条新规定。

derivatives.zh: 由 protest 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，义为「抗议者」
由拉丁词干 protestat- 加 -ion 构成，义为「声明；抗议」，语气正式
由 protesting 加 -ly 构成，义为「带着抗议地；不服地」

senses.title: A public expression of strong disagreement
senses.definition: a statement, gathering or march by which people show in public that they refuse to accept a decision or a situation
senses.definitionCN: 人们用声明、集会或游行的方式，公开表示不接受某项决定或某种状况
senses.example: The sit-in was a quiet protest against the closure of the library.
senses.exampleCN: 那次静坐是对关闭图书馆的一场无声抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to declare something publicly and call others to witness it; when the declaration is a refusal, the noun becomes the event in the street.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为公开声明并请人作证；当声明的内容是「不接受」时，名词就成了街头上的那场活动。

senses.title: To state in public that one objects
senses.definition: to say openly, often together with others, that something is wrong and ought to be changed
senses.definitionCN: 公开说出自己认为某事不对、应当改变，常与众人一起
senses.example: Villagers protested against the plan to dam the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民抗议在河上筑坝的计划。
senses.why: The same public declaration is now seen as an action rather than an event, so the verb keeps the crowd and the refusal but adds the doing.
senses.whyCN: 同一场公开声明被看成动作而不是事件，于是动词保留了人群与拒绝，只是多了一层「正在做」。

senses.title: To insist firmly that something is true
senses.definition: to say firmly that something is the case, especially when denying a charge or correcting what others believe
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地说某事就是这样，尤用于否认指控或纠正别人的看法
senses.example: He protested that he had never signed the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他坚称自己从未签过那份文件。
senses.why: Before it meant to object, the Latin verb simply meant to bear witness; that older layer survives whenever a person protests innocence rather than protesting a policy.
senses.whyCN: 在表示「反对」之前，这个拉丁动词只表示「作证」；一个人申辩自己无罪而不是抗议某项政策时，留下的正是那更早的一层。

intro.en: Protest goes back to a Latin verb for bearing witness in public; English first used it for a solemn declaration and only later for a refusal.
intro.cn: protest 可追到拉丁语中「公开作证」的动词；英语最初用它指郑重的声明，后来才用来指拒绝接受。

items.en: Testis meant a witness, the person who can stand up and say what happened.
items.cn: testis 意为证人，即那个能站出来说出发生了什么的人。

items.en: Testari meant to bear witness or to call someone as a witness, and it grew out of testis.
items.cn: testari 意为作证或请人作证，由 testis 派生而来。

items.en: With pro-, the witnessing moved into the open, so protestari meant to declare something publicly and solemnly.
items.cn: 加上 pro-，作证被推到公开场合，于是 protestari 意为公开而郑重地声明。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word as protest, a solemn declaration, and passed it into English around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语借入后写作 protest，意为郑重声明，约在十四世纪传入英语。

items.en: English kept the old sense of declaring, then added the modern one of objecting in public, and finally the quieter sense of insisting that one is right.
items.cn: 英语保留了「声明」的旧义，又添上「公开反对」的新义，最后还有「坚称自己没错」这层更安静的意思。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin witness and the declaration built on it; the second group gathers words for objecting and for stating a grievance.
note.cn: 第一组共用拉丁语的「证人」及由此构成的「声明」；第二组收表示反对与诉说不满的词。

entries.definition: A formal declaration, especially one that objects to something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的声明，尤指表示反对的声明。

entries.definition: To give evidence as a witness, from the same Latin word for witness.
entries.definitionCN: 作为证人提供证词，出自同一个表示「证人」的拉丁词。

entries.definition: A formal statement given by a witness in court.
entries.definitionCN: 证人在法庭上作出的正式陈述。

entries.definition: To keep someone safe; the prefix pro- is shared, but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 保护某人；只是拼写相近，词源不同，两者只共用前缀 pro-。

entries.definition: To say that you disagree with something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示不同意某事。

entries.definition: To gather in public in order to show opposition or support.
entries.definitionCN: 公开聚集以表示反对或支持。

entries.definition: A statement that something is wrong, often made to an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指出某事有问题的说法，常向当局提出。

entries.definition: A loud public expression of anger or disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 公众大声表达的愤怒或不满。

normalIntro.en: Every sense keeps the Latin witness: someone stands up in the open and says what he or she will not accept or will not admit.
normalIntro.cn: 每个义项都留着那个拉丁语的「证人」：有人站到明处，说出自己不接受或不承认的事。

normal.en: Pro- means forth and testis means witness, so protest is to bring a witness's statement out into public.
normal.cn: pro- 意为向前、公开，testis 意为证人，所以 protest 就是把证人的话拿到公开场合说出来。

normal.en: Testify, testimony and protest all keep that witness, which is why a courtroom and a street march can share one root.
normal.cn: testify、testimony 与 protest 都保留着这个「证人」，所以法庭与街头游行能共用一个词根。

normal.en: The noun names the event and the verb names the doing, yet both need other people to hear the refusal.
normal.cn: 名词指那场活动，动词指正在做的动作，但两者都需要别人听见这份拒绝。

normal.en: Protesting that you are innocent keeps the oldest sense, because there the word is still a declaration rather than a complaint.
normal.cn: 申辩自己无罪保留的是最古老的那层意思，因为那里它仍是声明，而不是抱怨。

normal.en: The stress moves with the part of speech in British English, and that shift alone tells a listener whether the word is the event or the act.
normal.cn: 英式英语里重音随词性移动，单是这一变化就能让听者知道这个词指事件还是动作。

abstract.en: A protest asks to be heard before it asks to be obeyed, which is why it lives in the open air.
abstract.cn: 抗议先求被听见，才求被采纳，所以它总发生在露天的场所。

abstract.en: The same word covers refusal and declaration because both are a person standing up and saying what is true for them.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指拒绝与声明，因为两者都是同一个人站出来，说出对他而言为真的事。

abstract.en: When a protest is ignored it tends to grow louder, while a declaration that is believed goes quiet, and one word holds both ends.
abstract.cn: 抗议被忽视时往往更响，声明被相信时反而安静，同一个词却装着这两端。

examples.en: Thousands joined the protest outside the town hall.
examples.cn: 数千人参加了市政厅外的抗议。

examples.en: They protested against the rise in bus fares.
examples.cn: 他们抗议公交车票价上涨。

examples.en: She protested that she had never met him.
examples.cn: 她坚称自己从未见过他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若泰斯特」——声音先「普」地一下炸开，再「泰斯特」地念出不满；记住 protest 是抗议、反对。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前、公开）+ testis（证人）→ testari（作证）→ protestari（公开声明、郑重宣称）→ 古法语 protest，约十四世纪进入英语。最早指「郑重声明」，后来才指「公开反对」。注意 protest 与 protect 只共用前缀 pro-：protect 的词根是 tegere（覆盖），protest 的词根是 testis（证人）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a public declaration; the senses divide into the event of objecting, the act of objecting, and the older sense of insisting on the truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「公开声明」；义项由此分出作为事件的抗议、作为动作的反对，以及更古老的「坚称事实」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd holding signs in front of a door, saying aloud what they will not accept.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群人举着纸牌站在门前，把不肯接受的事大声说出来。

branches.en: a row of signs lifted above a crowd
branches.cn: 人群上方举起的一排纸牌

branches.en: a chant rising outside a closed office
branches.cn: 紧闭的办公楼外响起整齐的喊声

branches.en: a man repeating that he never signed
branches.cn: 一个人反复说自己从未签过字

branches.en: one refusal spoken and acted at the same time
branches.cn: 同一份拒绝既被说出又被行动

branches.en: a word that objects and a word that swears
branches.cn: 一个既在反对又在申明的词

intro.en: A Latin noun for witness, a prefix that brings the statement into public, and the English endings that make the doer and the formal noun hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示「证人」的拉丁名词、把声明带到公开场合的前缀，以及造出「人」与正式名词的英语词尾，共同支撑这个词。

latinIntro.en: Testis, testari and protestari are the reliable Latin cognates; the same witness root also appears in testimony and testify.
latinIntro.cn: testis、testari 与 protestari 是可靠的同源词；同一个「证人」词根也出现在 testimony 与 testify 里。

definition_zh: 有能力的；能干的；能够…的
definition_en: having the ability or skill needed to do something
core_image: 一个人挽起袖子，双手稳稳接住递过来的任务
scene: 她一个人就能把这项工作做完。 She is capable of finishing the work on her own.
sceneCN: 这里 capable 是「有能力的」（第 1 个义项：具备做成某事的能力）；句意是她有能力独自完成这项工作。

derivatives.zh: capable 加 -ity 构成，义为「能力；性能」
capable 加 -ly 构成，义为「能干地」
in- 加 capable 构成，义为「无能力的」

senses.title: Having the skill to do something
senses.definition: able to do something well because of skill or experience
senses.definitionCN: 因具备技能或经验而能把事情做好
senses.example: She is a capable manager who solves problems quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位能干的经理，解决问题很快。
senses.why: Latin capere means to take or hold, so capable describes someone who can take a task in hand.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为「抓住、握住」，所以 capable 描写的是能把任务稳稳接在手里的人。

senses.title: Able to do or experience something
senses.definition: having the qualities or conditions needed for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 具备让某事发生所需要的性质或条件
senses.example: The material is capable of holding a great deal of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料能够储存大量热量。
senses.why: The idea of holding widens from people to things, so capable of can describe what an object can do.
senses.whyCN: 「容纳、握住」的想法从人扩展到物，所以 capable of 也能说明一个物体能做到什么。

intro.en: Capable comes from a Latin verb for taking hold, and its history explains why it pairs with of.
intro.cn: capable 来自拉丁语中表示「抓住」的动词，这段历史也解释了它为什么常与 of 搭配。

items.en: capere meant to take, to seize, or to hold, and it supplies the root cap-.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、抓、容纳」，提供了 cap- 这个词根。

items.en: capabilis was formed to mean able to hold or able to receive.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语造出 capabilis，意为「能容纳的、能接受的」。

items.en: The adjective passed into Old French as capable with the same sense of being fit to receive.
items.cn: 这个形容词以 capable 进入古法语，仍表示「能够接受、容纳」。

items.en: English borrowed it to describe a person or thing able to take in or undertake something.
items.cn: 英语借入后，用它描写能够接纳或承担某事的人或物。

items.en: The modern sense focuses on skill and ability, and the pattern be capable of became fixed.
items.cn: 现代义集中在技能与能力上，be capable of 的搭配也固定下来。

note.en: Capable sits in a large Latin family built on capere, and it is close in meaning to able and competent.
note.cn: capable 处在以 capere 为基础的大词族里，语义上又接近 able 与 competent。

entries.definition: the power or skill to do something
entries.definitionCN: 做成某事的能力或性能，由 capable 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: in a competent and effective way
entries.definitionCN: 能干地、有效地，由 capable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: not able to do something
entries.definitionCN: 无能力的，由否定前缀 in- 加 capable 构成。

entries.definition: having the power or skill to do something
entries.definitionCN: 有能力或技能做某事的，最常用的近义词。

entries.definition: having enough skill to do something properly
entries.definitionCN: 具备足够技能、能把事情做合格的。

entries.definition: having trained ability in a particular activity
entries.definitionCN: 在某一活动上受过训练、技术熟练的。

normalIntro.en: The root cap- means to take hold, so capable pictures someone who can take a task in hand.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 cap- 意为「抓住」，所以 capable 的画面是一个人能把任务接在手里。

normal.en: cap- comes from Latin capere, to take or hold.
normal.cn: cap- 来自拉丁语 capere，意为「拿、握住」。

normal.en: The suffix -able adds the sense of being able to do that holding.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 补上「能够做到」的意思。

normal.en: capability is the noun beside it, and capability and capable share the same stem.
normal.cn: 名词 capability 就在旁边，它与 capable 共用同一个词干。

normal.en: The fixed pattern is be capable of doing, with a gerund rather than a bare verb.
normal.cn: 固定句型是 be capable of doing，后面接动名词而不是动词原形。

normal.en: The opposite is incapable, built with the negative prefix in-.
normal.cn: 反义词是 incapable，用否定前缀 in- 构成。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands opening to receive a heavy box and holding it steady.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手张开接住一个重箱子，并稳稳托住。

abstract.en: Picture a tool that fits the hand so well that the work almost does itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一件工具与手贴合得极好，活儿几乎自己就完成了。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked capable that opens when a task is pushed against it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着 capable 的门，任务一推就开。

examples.en: She is capable of finishing the work on her own.
examples.cn: 她有能力独自完成这项工作。

examples.en: He is a capable manager who solves problems quickly.
examples.cn: 他是一位能干的经理，解决问题很快。

examples.en: This material is capable of holding a great deal of heat.
examples.cn: 这种材料能够储存大量热量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开牌」——手里的牌一摊开，什么任务都接得住。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓住、容纳）+ -abilis（能…的）→ 晚期拉丁语 capabilis → 古法语 capable。

sensesIntro.en: One root meaning to hold branches into personal skill and into what a thing can do.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示「容纳、握住」的词根，分叉出人的技能和物的性能两条义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands taking hold of a task and holding it without dropping it.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手接住一项任务，并且稳稳托住不掉。

branches.en: The personal sense: a person with the skill to handle work.
branches.cn: 指人的义项：具备处理工作技能的人。

branches.en: The extended sense: a thing with the properties needed for an effect.
branches.cn: 扩展义：具备产生某种效果所需性质的物。

branches.en: Both senses keep the original image of holding something within reach.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留着「把东西握在可及之处」的原始画面。

branches.en: In appraisal, capable is a solid compliment without the force of brilliant.
branches.cn: 在评价里，capable 是稳妥的褒义，没有 brilliant 那么强烈。

branches.en: Technical writing uses capable of to state what a material or system can do.
branches.cn: 技术写作常用 capable of 说明材料或系统能做什么。

intro.en: Capable is an adjective built from the root cap- plus the suffix -able.
intro.cn: capable 是由词根 cap- 加后缀 -able 构成的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere, to take or hold, is one of the most productive roots in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere（拿、握住）是英语中构词能力最强的词根之一。

items.meaning: able to do or hold something
items.example: She is capable of great patience.
items.exampleCN: 她能够表现出极大的耐心。

items.meaning: the power or skill to do something
items.example: The team has the capability to deliver on time.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队有能力按时交付。
她干练地处理了这起投诉。

items.example: He was incapable of making a decision.

items.meaning: to take, to seize, to hold
items.example: Capere is the source of many English words.
items.exampleCN: capere 是许多英语单词的来源。

items.example: The bag is capacious enough for a laptop.
items.exampleCN: 这个包大到能装下一台笔记本电脑。

items.meaning: to take something that is offered
items.example: She accepted the invitation at once.
The story captivated the whole class.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事让全班听得入迷。

latinEntries.meaning: to take, to seize, to hold

definition_zh: 系统；体系；制度；方法
definition_en: a set of connected parts or rules working together
core_image: 地铁线路图上纵横交错的彩色线条汇成一个网络
scene: 这座城市的地铁系统非常方便。 The city s metro system is very convenient.

senses.title: Connected parts working together
senses.definition: a group of parts that operate as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体运作的一组部件
senses.example: The city s metro system is very convenient.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的地铁系统非常方便。
senses.why: The Greek word meant an organized whole, which is exactly the modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词意为有组织的整体，正是现代的含义。

senses.title: An established set of rules
senses.definition: an organized set of rules or customs
senses.definitionCN: 一套有组织的规则或惯例
senses.example: The tax system favours small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 税制对小企业有利。
senses.why: Rules arranged into a working whole are a system in the same sense as machinery.
senses.whyCN: 规则被安排成运作的整体，与机械系统同理。

senses.title: An organized method
senses.definition: a planned way of doing something
senses.definitionCN: 有计划的行事方式
senses.example: She has a system for taking notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一套记笔记的方法。
senses.why: A personal routine can also be an organized whole, so the word covers method.
senses.whyCN: 个人习惯也能构成有组织的整体，因此这个词也指方法。

senses.title: The body as a whole
senses.definition: the body or one of its functional groups
senses.definitionCN: 身体或其中某个功能组
senses.example: Exercise strengthens the immune system.
senses.exampleCN: 锻炼增强免疫系统。
senses.why: The body is the most literal set of connected parts, so its groups are also systems.
senses.whyCN: 身体是最字面的相连部件集合，因此其各类功能组也叫系统。

items.en: Late Latin systema named an arranged whole.

items.en: French systeme carried the ordered sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 systeme 把有序整体的含义带入英语。

items.en: System extended to rules, methods and the body.

definition_zh: 樱桃；樱桃树；樱桃色；樱桃木
definition_en: a small round red or dark red fruit with a single hard stone, or the tree that bears it
core_image: 枝头垂着的小红果，咬开是甜汁和一枚硬核
scene: 初夏的果园里，孩子们踮起脚尖伸手去够枝头最红的那一颗。 She picked the ripest cherry from the tree and ate it on the spot.
sceneCN: 这里 cherry 是「樱桃」（第 1 个义项：樱桃树的果实）；句意是「她从树上摘下最熟的那颗樱桃，当场吃了」。

senses.title: The edible fruit of the cherry tree
senses.definition: a small round fruit with red or dark red skin, sweet or sour flesh, and a single hard stone
senses.definitionCN: 一种小圆果，皮呈红色或深红，果肉甜或酸，中间有一枚硬核
senses.example: The cake was topped with cream and a single cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上点缀着奶油和一颗樱桃。
senses.why: The word names the fruit itself, so the core image is the round red berry hanging on the branch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指的就是果实本身，核心意象是挂在枝头的小红果。

senses.title: The tree that bears cherries
senses.definition: the tree (genus Prunus) that produces cherries, grown for fruit or for blossom
senses.definitionCN: 结樱桃的树（李属），种来收果或赏花
senses.example: They planted a cherry in the garden years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 多年前他们在花园里种了一棵樱桃树。
senses.why: English routinely extends fruit names to the plant itself, so the berry image grows into the tree.
senses.whyCN: 英语习惯把果名直接延伸到果树本身，果实意象便扩展成整棵树。

senses.title: The wood of the cherry tree
senses.definition: the reddish-brown timber of the cherry tree, valued for furniture and cabinets
senses.definitionCN: 樱桃树的木材，呈红棕色，常用于做家具和柜子
senses.example: The cabinet is made of solid cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个柜子是实心樱桃木做的。
senses.why: Material names in English often come from the tree source, extending the image from fruit to timber.
senses.whyCN: 英语里木材名常直接取自树名，意象从果实延伸到木材。

senses.title: A bright red colour like a cherry
senses.definition: a bright red colour resembling ripe cherries, often used of lips, paint or fabrics
senses.definitionCN: 像熟樱桃一样的鲜红色，常用来形容嘴唇、油漆或布料
senses.example: Her new scarf was a glossy cherry.
senses.exampleCN: 她的新围巾是亮泽的樱桃红色。
senses.why: The intense red skin of the fruit becomes a colour name, a common path in colour vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 果实鲜红的果皮被借为颜色名，这是颜色词汇最常见的形成路径。

senses.title: The hymen, in informal or euphemistic use
senses.definition: in informal slang, virginity, especially in the phrase to lose one's cherry
senses.definitionCN: 在俚语中委婉指童贞，常见于 lose one's cherry 一语
senses.example: That slang sense appears mainly in very informal speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俚语义主要出现在非常口语的场合。
senses.why: The round red shape invites euphemistic slang, a figurative leap from fruit to taboo topic.
senses.whyCN: 红圆的果形引发了委婉俚语，从果实意象跳跃到禁忌话题。

senses.title: The best part or prize, in figurative use
senses.titleCN: 精华；最好的部分（比喻用法）
senses.definition: figuratively, the best or most attractive thing, as in the cherry on the cake
senses.definitionCN: 比喻最精彩、最诱人的部分，如 the cherry on the cake（锦上添花之物）
senses.example: Winning the award was the cherry on top of a great season.
senses.exampleCN: 获奖是精彩赛季锦上添花的一笔。
senses.why: The sweet red fruit placed on top of a dessert stands for the finishing touch, hence the best part.
senses.whyCN: 甜点顶端那颗红樱桃象征点睛之笔，由此引申为最好的部分。

intro.en: Cherry is one of the many fruit words English borrowed through French from Latin, and the singular form was reshaped by folk etymology.
intro.cn: cherry 是英语经法语借自拉丁语的众多果名之一，其单数形式还曾被民间词源重新塑造。

items.en: Latin had cerasus (or ceresium), the cherry tree and its fruit, borrowed from Greek kerasos; the ultimate source is possibly an Anatolian language, though this is generally considered uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语有 cerasus（或 ceresium），指樱桃树及其果实，借自希腊语 kerasos；更早的来源一般认为不确定，可能出自安纳托利亚语系语言。

items.en: Latin cerasum evolved into Old French cerise, which Anglo-Norman speakers brought to England after 1066.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cerasum 演变为古法语 cerise，1066 年之后随盎格鲁-诺曼人带入英格兰。

items.en: The word appears in Middle English as cherise or cheryse; because the final s was heard as a plural ending, speakers cut it off and the singular cherry was formed by mistake, a classic folk etymology.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 cherise / cheryse；词尾的 s 被误当成复数标记，人们把它剪掉，错误地造出了单数 cherry，是典型的民间词源现象。

items.en: The plural cherries was re-formed from the new singular, and the tree sense and the timber sense became established as English gardeners and cabinetmakers used the word daily.
items.cn: 复数 cherries 从新的单数重新生成，果树义和木材义随着园丁和木匠的日常使用而固定下来。

items.en: Colour names, figurative phrases such as the cherry on the cake, and the compound cherry-pick all grew from the fruit image.
items.cn: 颜色名、the cherry on the cake 等比喻短语，以及复合词 cherry-pick，都是从果实意象生长出来的。

note.en: Cherry belongs to a small family of fruit-and-tree words, and it is easy to confuse with visually similar English words.
note.cn: cherry 属于一小组「果实＋树木」词，也容易和拼写或发音相近的英语词混淆。

entries.definition: to love and care for something deeply
entries.definitionCN: 珍爱；珍视——开头字母与 cherry 相同，但词源无关，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: happy and cheerful in manner
entries.definitionCN: 欢快的；兴致高的——与 cherry 仅一个字母之差，词源不同

entries.definition: a bright red colour, borrowed directly from French
entries.definitionCN: 樱桃红——cherry 的古法语前身 cerise 直接借入英语成为颜色词

entries.definition: a small juicy fruit without a stone, such as a strawberry or blueberry
entries.definitionCN: 浆果——同为小型果实，但 berry 无硬核，cherry 有核

entries.definition: a soft round fruit with yellow-pink skin and a large stone
entries.definitionCN: 桃——同为核果，果形更大，也常进入比喻用法

entries.definition: a juicy oval fruit with a single stone, purple or red when ripe
entries.definitionCN: 李子——同属李属核果，与樱桃亲缘关系很近

normalIntro.en: Use the word's shape, sound and word family to lock it in.
normalIntro.cn: 用词形、读音和词族把 cherry 牢牢记住。

normal.en: cherry ends in -erry like berry and merry, a rhyming trio of small happy words.
normal.cn: cherry 词尾 -erry 与 berry（浆果）、merry（欢乐）押韵，三个轻快的小词一组。

normal.en: Old French cerise lost its s because English heard it as a plural, so cherry is cerise minus the mistaken ending.
normal.cn: 古法语 cerise 的 s 被误当复数剪掉，cherry 就是「cerise 去掉错认的词尾」。

normal.en: Plural cherries changes y to i before -es, the same spelling rule as babies and cities.
normal.cn: 复数 cherries 把 y 变 i 再加 es，规则同 babies、cities。

normal.en: Cherry blossom is the famous spring image; the tree sense lives in this phrase.
normal.cn: cherry blossom（樱花）是著名的春日意象，树的义项就藏在这个短语里。

normal.en: Cherry-pick means to take only the best, the fruit picked by hand.
normal.cn: cherry-pick 意为「只挑最好的」，即亲手摘果的意象。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny red globe with a green stem, the exact image the word carries.
abstract.cn: 想一颗带绿梗的小红球，这正是这个词的核心画面。

abstract.en: See a cake crowned by one cherry: the finishing touch, the best part.
abstract.cn: 看蛋糕顶上那颗樱桃：点睛之笔，最好的部分。

abstract.en: Hear the rhyme cherry–berry–merry as three stones skipping on water.
abstract.cn: 把 cherry–berry–merry 的韵脚想象成水上连跳的三颗小石子。

examples.en: She picked the ripest cherry from the tree and ate it on the spot.
examples.cn: 她从树上摘下最熟的那颗樱桃，当场吃了。

examples.en: The avenue is lined with cherry trees that bloom in April.
examples.cn: 街道两旁种着四月开花的樱桃树。

examples.en: Being named captain was the cherry on top of a perfect season.
examples.cn: 被任命为队长是完美赛季锦上添花的一笔。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拆粒」——把枝头的小红果一颗颗拆下来吃，一拆一粒，就是 cherry（樱桃）。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 cerasus（樱桃树／樱桃），经古法语 cerise 进入英语；拉丁语词又借自希腊语 kerasos，更早来源可能出自安纳托利亚地区的语言，具体存疑。英语把词尾 s 误当复数剪掉，形成单数 cherry，属民间词源。与 cher只是词源同源，与 cherish、cheery 仅拼写相近。

sensesIntro.en: From the fruit itself, the word spreads naturally to the tree, its timber, its colour, and then into slang and figurative uses.
sensesIntro.cn: 从果实本身出发，词义自然扩展到樱桃树、樱桃木、樱桃红色，再进入俚语和比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small round red fruit with one hard stone hanging from a branch
core.cn: 核心意象：枝头垂着的一颗小圆红果，咬开有一枚硬核

branches.en: the fruit itself, eaten fresh or as dessert topping
branches.cn: 果实本身，鲜食或作甜点缀

branches.en: the tree that bears the fruit, from orchard to blossom
branches.cn: 结出果实的樱桃树，从果园到樱花

branches.en: the wood and the colour both borrowed from the fruit's appearance
branches.cn: 木材与颜色都借自果实的外观

branches.en: slang euphemism grown from the fruit's shape
branches.cn: 由果形引出的俚语委婉用法

branches.en: figurative use: the cherry on top as the best part
branches.cn: 比喻用法：顶上那颗樱桃即最好的部分

intro.en: Cherry is a simple loanword rather than a built-up derivative, so its affix notes focus on the French source, its colour relative, and the compounds it has formed in English.
intro.cn: cherry 是单纯借词而非层层派生的产物，构词说明聚焦法语来源、同源颜色词，以及它在英语中形成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestor cerasus left a few descendants in European languages; the clearest relative in English is cerise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语祖源 cerasus 在欧洲各语言留下少量后裔，英语中最清晰的同源词是 cerise。

items.meaningCN: 樱桃树；樱桃（拉丁语源头词）
items.example: Latin cerasus came from Greek kerasos.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cerasus 借自希腊语 kerasos。

items.meaningCN: 樱桃树（希腊语中介来源）
items.example: Greek kerasos is the direct source of the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语 kerasos 是拉丁语词的直接来源。

items.structure: Old French noun, borrowed into English
items.meaningCN: 樱桃红；樱桃（古法语原形）
items.exampleCN: 她穿了一条樱桃红的裙子。

items.meaning: the flowers of the cherry tree
items.example: Tourists gather to view the cherry blossom each spring.
items.exampleCN: 每年春天游客们赶来赏樱。

items.example: A cherry tree stood by the gate.

items.meaning: to choose only the best or most profitable items
items.example: Critics accused the report of cherry-picking data.
items.exampleCN: 批评者指责该报告挑拣数据。

items.meaning: a bright red like ripe cherries
items.example: The car was painted cherry red.

items.meaning: a tart variety of cherry used in cooking
items.example: The pie is made with sour cherries.
items.exampleCN: 这个派是用酸樱桃做的。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 樱桃果实（古法语 cerise 的直接来源）

derivatives.zh: 由 cherry（樱桃）加 pick（挑选）构成，义为「挑肥拣瘦，只挑最好的」

definition_zh: 文学的；文学性的；书面的；从事文学的
definition_en: relating to literature or to writing valued as art, and also describing a formal bookish style rather than everyday speech
core_image: 一盏台灯下摊开的旧小说，纸页边缘被手指翻得发软
scene: 深夜的书房里，台灯照着摊开的旧小说，读的人反复摩挲着发软的纸页。 Her literary taste was shaped by the novels she read late at night.
sceneCN: 这里 literary 是「文学的」（第 1 个义项：与文学作品有关）；句意为她的文学品味是深夜读小说时养成的。图中可辨识物件：台灯、旧小说、发软的纸页。

pos.zh: 文学的；文学性的；书面的；从事文学的

collocations.zh: 文稿代理人；文学经纪人

derivatives.zh: 与 literary 同出拉丁语 littera（字母），义为「文学；文献」
由同一词干加 -ate 构成，义为「有读写能力的；有文化的」
由同一词干加 -cy 构成，义为「读写能力」

senses.title: Relating to literature
senses.definition: connected with literature, especially novels, poems and plays that are valued as art
senses.definitionCN: 与文学有关的，尤指与被视为艺术的小说、诗歌和戏剧有关
senses.example: She has a keen literary taste and reads a novel every week.
senses.exampleCN: 她文学品味敏锐，每周读一本小说。
senses.why: Latin littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and writing made of letters grew into literature; literary simply points back to that body of writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 littera 意为字母，由字母写成的文字逐渐长成文学；literary 就是回头指向这一整片写作。

senses.title: Typical of formal written language
senses.definition: of a word or style, formal and at home in books rather than in ordinary conversation
senses.definitionCN: 指词语或文风正式，常见于书本，而不用于日常对话
senses.example: The word behold is literary rather than conversational.
senses.exampleCN: behold 这个词是书面语，而不是日常口语。
senses.why: A word that has left the street but survives in books is labelled by the place where it still lives; literary records the shelf, not the age of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一个词从街头消失却仍在书中存活，就被按它如今的栖身之处来标注；literary 记下的是书架，不是这个词的年岁。

senses.title: Having the quality of artful writing
senses.definition: showing the imagination and craft associated with good literature
senses.definitionCN: 显出与优秀文学作品相联系的想象力与写作技艺
senses.example: His account of the journey has a literary quality that makes it memorable.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这次旅程的记述有一种文学性的质地，让人读过难忘。
senses.why: Literature is writing judged for craft as well as content; when a passage invites that judgment, the adjective follows it from the shelf into the sentence.
senses.whyCN: 文学是既看内容也看手笔的文字；当一段话引来这种品评时，这个形容词便跟着它从书架走进句子，形容那段文字本身的质地。

senses.title: Connected with the profession of letters
senses.titleCN: 从事文学的；文学工作的
senses.definition: involving writers, books and the business or study that surrounds them, as in a literary agent or a literary magazine
senses.definitionCN: 涉及作家、书籍以及围绕它们的行业或研究，如文学经纪人、文学杂志
senses.example: The literary agent read the manuscript and offered a contract.
senses.exampleCN: 那位文学经纪人读完稿子，给了出版合同。
senses.why: Books support a small industry of editors, agents and magazines; literary names that professional world because it exists to produce and sell literature.
senses.whyCN: 书籍养活了编辑、经纪人和杂志组成的小行业；literary 指的就是这个职业圈子，因为它的存在就是为了生产和销售文学。

intro.en: Literary descends from the Latin word for a letter, and it still points to writing that is made of letters and valued as art.
intro.cn: literary 源自拉丁语中表示「字母」的词，至今仍指向由字母写成、并被当作艺术来欣赏的文字。

items.en: Littera named a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural it could name a written document or an epistle.
items.cn: littera 指字母表中的一个字母，复数形式还可指文书或书信。

items.en: The adjective litterarius meant of letters or of writing, and it covered both the skill of reading and the study of texts.
items.cn: 形容词 litterarius 意为与字母、书写有关的，既指读写技能，也指对文本的研究。

items.en: Old French reshaped the Latin adjective as literaire, keeping the sense of letters, learning and written culture.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁形容词改写为 literaire，保留了文字、学问与书面文化的意味。

items.en: English borrowed the French form as literary in the seventeenth century, when literature was coming to mean fine writing rather than learning in general.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语借入法语形式，写作 literary；当时 literature 正从泛指学问转向指精美的写作。

items.en: Modern English keeps literary for the art of writing, for its formal register, and for the people and institutions that surround books.
items.cn: 现代英语用 literary 指写作的艺术、其正式语体，以及围绕书籍的人和机构。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin word for a letter; the near-meaning group gathers words for writing, art and books.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」一词上的词；近义组收表示写作、艺术与书籍的词。

entries.definition: Written works valued as art, or the body of writing on a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 文学；文献；与 literary 同出拉丁语 littera。

entries.definition: Able to read and write.
entries.definitionCN: 有读写能力的；来自同一拉丁词干。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力；由同一词干加 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: Following the exact words rather than an intended meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 字面的；按字面理解的；同样来自 littera，但走的是另一条语义分支。

entries.definition: Set down in writing rather than spoken.
entries.definitionCN: 写下来的；书面形式的。

entries.definition: Showing creative skill and a sense of beauty.
entries.definitionCN: 有艺术性的；显出创造才能与美感的。

entries.definition: Relating to poetry, or having its beauty and rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 与诗歌有关的；富有诗意与韵律的。

entries.definition: Fond of reading and study, or describing language taken from books.
entries.definitionCN: 爱读书的；书卷气的；也指从书本里搬来的语言。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in the Latin name for a letter, and its family keeps returning to reading, writing and the art of books.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在拉丁语对「字母」的称呼上，它的同族词反复回到阅读、书写与书本的艺术。

normal.en: Latin littera is a letter, so literature is writing made of letters and literary is what belongs to that writing.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 littera 是字母，所以 literature 是由字母写成的文字，literary 则指属于这种文字的东西。

normal.en: Literature and literary share one stem: the noun names the whole body of works, the adjective describes what belongs to it.
normal.cn: literature 与 literary 共用一个词干：名词指整批作品，形容词描述属于这批作品的东西。

normal.en: Literate and literacy also come from the letter, because knowing the letters is the first step into reading.
normal.cn: literate 与 literacy 也来自「字母」，因为认识字母是进入阅读的第一步。

normal.en: A literary agent handles books as a business, so the adjective also names the profession built around literature.
normal.cn: 文学经纪人把书当作生意来经营，所以这个形容词也指围绕文学形成的职业。

normal.en: Call a word literary when you meet it mainly in books, because the label records where the word still lives.
normal.cn: 一个词若主要是在书里遇到，就叫它 literary，因为这个标签记下的是它如今还住在哪里。

abstract.en: Letters are small marks that carry whole worlds, and literary is the adjective for the world built out of those marks.
abstract.cn: 字母是承载整个世界的小小记号，literary 就是形容由这些记号搭起来的那个世界。

abstract.en: A page can be read for information or for beauty; literary marks the second use.
abstract.cn: 一页纸可以为了信息去读，也可以为了美去读；literary 标出的是后一种读法。

abstract.en: Every literature begins with someone learning a handful of letters, which is why the same root also names literacy.
abstract.cn: 每一部文学都从有人学会几个字母开始，所以同一个词根也用来指读写能力。

examples.en: She has a keen literary taste and reads a novel every week.
examples.cn: 她文学品味敏锐，每周读一本小说。

examples.en: His account of the journey has a literary quality that makes it memorable.
examples.cn: 他对这次旅程的记述有一种文学性的质地，让人读过难忘。

examples.en: The literary agent read the manuscript and offered a contract.
examples.cn: 那位文学经纪人读完稿子，给了出版合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特瑞」——姓李的人特别爱读小说，身上有股文学的味儿；literary 就是文学的。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母、文字）→ litterarius（与文字有关的）→ 古法语 literaire → 英语 literary；同族词多与字母、读写、文学有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is writing made of letters and valued as art; the senses divide into the art itself, its formal register, its crafted quality, and the profession around books.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是由字母写成、被当作艺术的文字；义项由此分出文学本身、它的正式语体、它的写作技艺，以及围绕书籍的职业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old novel open under a lamp, its pages softened by repeated reading.
core.cn: 核心意象：台灯下摊开的旧小说，纸页被反复翻读得发软。

branches.en: a reader turning the soft pages of an old novel
branches.cn: 读者翻动旧小说发软的纸页

branches.en: a literary agent's desk piled with manuscripts
branches.cn: 文学经纪人的桌上堆满稿件

branches.en: a word that lives only in books
branches.cn: 一个只在书里活着的词

branches.en: a sentence polished until it sounds like music
branches.cn: 一句话被磨到听起来像音乐

branches.en: a description that makes a plain road feel alive
branches.cn: 一段让普通道路活起来的描写

intro.en: A Latin word for a letter, its adjective, one French reshaping and two English suffixes carry literary from the alphabet to the art of books.
intro.cn: 一个表示字母的拉丁词、它的形容词、一次法语改写，再加两个英语后缀，把 literary 从字母表带到书本的艺术。

latinIntro.en: Littera and litterarius are recorded Latin words, and the adjective reached English through French before it was reshaped as literary.
latinIntro.cn: littera 与 litterarius 都是有记录的拉丁词；这个形容词经法语进入英语，后来才改写为 literary。

items.meaning: the ability to read and write

latinEntries.meaningCN: 文字写作；由文字得来的学问
